A spokesperson for Talarico told Snopes via email that Talarico voted nay on SB 17 to avoid giving the governor increased power. Talarico's team elaborated: James doesn't support the Chinese Communist Party owning Texas land and his record reflects that, including by voting to stop countries like China from purchasing land near critical infrastructure like military bases. Ken Paxton is spreading lies about bills that sought to ban American citizens from buying land in this country — undermining our neighbors' God-given rights — in an effort to distract from his career of corruption. Paxton is the only candidate in this race that has cozied up to the Chinese Communist Party, going on a lavish all-expenses-paid trip to China and meeting with CCP officials while he was supposed to be serving us. There's a reason Republicans call him "Commie Ken." The bill ultimately passed and was signed into law in September 2025. The record also showed Talarico had voted yea previously on one of the amendments of the bill aimed at protecting U.S. visa holders, but ultimately voted nay on the final bill. SB 667 and other related votes Legislators voted on a different bill, SB 667 , aimed at "prohibiting state entities from investing in Chinese-affiliated entities" as a means of funding state-funded pension plans on May 28, 2025. According to the Texas House Journal transcript of that meeting, Talarico had an excused absence that day and did not vote on the final version of the bill, which ultimately passed. Talarico's votes on other bills with potential impact on Texans' dealings with foreign entities included: Yea on SB 1349 , which was part of the legislative package that included SB 17, described as "creating the criminal offenses of transnational repression and unauthorized enforcement of foreign law." (The House Journal shows Talarico as first voting nay, with a correction that it was meant to be recorded as yea.) Yea on SB 2116 , which was aimed at "business or governmental entities from entering into contracts or other agreements relating to state critical infrastructure with certain foreign-owned companies." Yea on HB 130 , aimed at preventing the "use of biotechnology by foreign adversary countries as a component of military power and commercial advantage. The "Commie Ken" reference in the statement from Talarico's team referenced to a 2023 report that alleged Paxton went on a "lavish" trip to China to meet with government officials, reportedly against the advice of his staff. Paxton's opponent in the 2026 Texas Republican primary, incumbent four-term Sen. John Cornyn, called out Paxton's trip during his campaign and even built a website called CrookedKen.com that also labeled him "Commie Ken" and described him as "cozying up to the CCP." For further reading, we've investigated other claims about Talarico, including that he once said he "hated" Christianity and that U.S. President Donald Trump once called him an "insult to Jesus."

title: Trump didn't post about building 'Melania Canal,' despite claims
label: Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating
text: Claim: A screenshot authentically shows a Truth Social post from U.S. President Donald Trump announcing the construction of the "Melania Canal" to connect to "Lake America," also known as Lake Ontario. Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating After U.S. President Donald Trump announced in August 2026 that he would rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America," social media users spread a screenshot appearing to show a Truth Social post from the president that announced the construction of the "Melania Canal" that would connect to the lake. The screenshot circulated across Facebook ( screenshot ) and Threads . Here's what Trump allegedly said: The FAKE NEWS is saying we need the Canadian canals that connect to LAKE AMERICA. Total lie! We don't need their small, low-energy Welland Canal! America built the Panama Canal, we built the Suez Canal — incredible, beautiful, high-IQ canals! I have officially instructed the Army Corps of Engineers to build a much BIGGER, DEEPER, WIDER, and far more powerful canal bypass connecting straight into Lake America! It is going to be magnificent! And we are naming it after my stunning, beautiful wife: THE MELANIA CANAL. Every American will be able to EASILY enter the Melania Canal from BOTH the front end and the back side for a very minimal fee! Thank you for your attention to this matter. Some users seemed to interpret the rumor as true, and Snopes readers contacted us to investigate its legitimacy. A closer look at the screenshot indicated that this post was labeled as satire, both under the usual spot for "Likes" on a Truth Social post and as a watermark across the image. According to the watermark, this post originated with a Facebook account called Mrs. Putin, which identifies itself as "Satire/Parody" in its description. Mrs. Putin first shared the post ( screenshot ) on Aug. 29. As Mrs. Putin pointed out in a Facebook message conversation with Snopes in 2025, the account's posts often include several indicators that they are satire, including misspelled names. In this case, aside from the "satire" label, other indicators that the post is fake include that Mrs. Putin changed "Likes" to "disLikes" and misspelled Trump's social media tag, "@realDonaldTrump," as "@realDotardTurmp" and his last name as Turmp. (Mrs. Putin) A search of Trump's social media accounts using the databases Trump's Truth and Factbase also determined that, as of this writing, the president has not declared the construction of a "Melania Canal." He did, however, float renaming the Strait of Hormuz to "Trump Strait" in a Sept. 2 Truth Social post . For more on Lake Ontario and its renaming, Snopes previously debunked a claim that Canadian officials were refusing passage to ships with "Lake America" in their documentation and confirmed that Lake Ontario was not named after the Canadian province . Snopes also has previously written about numerous satirical Mrs. Putin posts. Because the effectiveness of satire is subjective , we use " originated as satire " or " labeled satire " ratings based on creators' description of their work. It's your call on whether you agree.

title: What former White House chef Andre Rush has said about Trump's work ethic, demeanor
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: Former White House chef Andre Rush said Trump is a "worker" who is always friendly to the staff. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True In one interview published by a credible source, Rush said about Trump, "He's a worker. He's up all night." In another interview Rush said Trump "does try to eat healthy, but people don't get to see that part of it. They just see the part that we want to show on social media." What's Undetermined Tabloid news outlet TMZ paraphrased a comment it ascribed to Rush as, "Trump was always friendly and complimentary to the staff," but didn't present it as a direct quote. We have reached out to Rush for confirmation and will update this story accordingly. In late August and early September 2026, numerous Facebook posts purported to quote Andre Rush, a former White House chef , praising U.S. President Donald Trump for his work ethic, healthy diet and friendliness to the White House staff. Snopes readers sent us examples of the post in which three separated quotes were attributed to Rush. Below are the various sections of the post the alleged Rush quotes in bold (emphasis ours): Chef Andre Rush. Nearly 20 years working inside the White House kitchen. Four Presidents. Clinton. Bush. Obama. Trump. A man who observed all of them from extremely close range — not from a press conference, not from a campaign rally — but from the most personal place imaginable. Their kitchen. Because you can say anything in a speech. You can put on a performance at a rally. You can create an image for the cameras. But inside a kitchen — at unusual hours — when food is being prepared and nobody important is paying attention — that is where the real person can reveal themselves. And here is what Chef Rush reportedly revealed — something the media reduced to one sentence before moving on. When he was asked which President was the most difficult to cook for — he said Trump. But not for the reason you might expect. "He's a worker. He's up all night. It wasn't a lot of morning breakfast." Up all night. The kitchen was prepared. The meals were ready. And Trump simply wasn't there to eat them. Because he was working. […] The chef could never predict when Trump would walk through that kitchen. Because Trump's schedule wasn't organized around meals. It was organized around America. And when Trump DID come through the kitchen? "Always friendly. Always complimentary to the staff." Not once — during all those years — did Trump make the kitchen staff feel unimportant. Never a cruel word. Never an unreasonable demand. Never the kind of behavior powerful people sometimes display when they believe nobody significant is watching. […] And then Rush said the part that completely broke me. "He does try to eat healthy. People don't get to see that part. They just see what we want to show on social media." For years, the media showed you Trump eating McDonald's. The Diet Coke. Image after image that could make him appear careless. But his own chef — the man who actually prepared his food — said publicly that Trump tries. That the real picture is different from what people see online. Although placed in a highly embellished context above, two of the highlighted quotes about Rush's experience working in Trump's White House were taken from credible published sources. The alleged quote about Trump's friendliness was actually a paraphrase of remarks attributed to Rush by TMZ, a tabloid news outlet. Snopes reached out to Rush via Instagram to confirm these quotes and will update this story accordingly. Until then, we rate this claim a mixture of true and undetermined information. Other parts of the post are elaborate descriptions that may or may not have derived from things Rush actually said. For example, we have not found evidence that Rush said , "Not once — during all those years — did Trump make the kitchen staff feel unimportant." Nor did we find proof that Rush said Trump never said a " cruel word " or made an " unreasonable demand ." Rush worked as a chef at the White House for nearly 20 years, cooking for former presidents Bill Clinton, George W. Bush and Barack Obama, as well as during the first Trump administration. In a 2021 interview with Mashed , a cooking and food service publication, he spoke about Trump's meal habits: He's a worker. He's up all night. It wasn't a lot of morning breakfast. Actually, all of them [the presidents], it was very different in comparison. Food wasn't a high priority, when I say that, I mean on the administration side of it — on that administration side of it for his term. Nothing's wrong with that if you know what he ate and how he ate during the day, which has been all over from the burgers to everything overcooked or taco salads. … I would have to say burgers would be the number one if I had to put [it] into perspective, as he'd call it the American food. In a 2024 interview with Politico, Rush described Trump's eating habits: He gets so much flack about the unhealthy side of him. He does try to eat healthy, but people don't get to see that part of it. They just see the part that we want to show on social media. I mean, Bill Clinton ate just as many burgers as Donald Trump did. In a 2024 interview with TMZ, Rush allegedly said Trump was always friendly and complimentary with the staff. However, TMZ did not directly quote Rush and appears to have paraphrased his words: Rush made sure to note Trump was always friendly and complimentary to the kitchen staff … which the chef is sure will continue — even if the cooks have to covertly slip veggies into his meals. Snopes has previously reported on rumors about Trump's diet and health , including the claim that he uses a button in his office to order Diet Cokes .

title: Did Trump order that weeping willows be cut down outside Kennedy Center?
label: Rating: False About this rating
text: Claim: In the summer of 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump ordered the removal of weeping willow trees outside the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C. Rating: False About this rating Context Matthew Floca, the Kennedy Center's vice president of facilities, said in April 2026 sworn testimony that the center felled its weeping willows "because they were falling down." He also confirmed Trump was not involved in the decision. In late August and early September 2026, a claim ( archived ) circulated online that U.S. President Donald Trump ordered the removal of weeping willow trees outside the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C. "The iconic weeping willow trees outside the Kennedy Center have been cut down by Trump," Adam Parkhomenko, a former Hillary Clinton adviser, wrote on X . The iconic weeping willow trees outside the Kennedy Center have been cut down by Trump. pic.twitter.com/5bZ0AnaPDx — Adam Parkhomenko (@AdamParkhomenko) September 1, 2026 Similar claims also circulated on Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), Threads ( archived ), Bluesky ( archived ) and Reddit ( archived ). Snopes readers contacted us to verify them. One reader asked, "Did Trump have the willow trees at the JFK center cut down?" That was not the case. Rather, Matthew Floca , the Kennedy Center's vice president of facilities, said in April 2026 sworn testimony that the center felled its weeping willows "because they were falling down" (Page 27). Floca's testimony was part of a lawsuit seeking to block Trump's planned renovations of the center. Floca said in his testimony that the center felled the trees because of a "maintenance need" (Page 28) and that it was "contemplating" their replacements. Floca added that he had not spoken to Trump, who is the chair of the Kennedy Center Board of Trustees, about the weeping willows or what should replace them (Page 28). Given the above, we rate the claim that Trump ordered the removal of the Kennedy Center's weeping willow trees false. Rather, the center's management said it felled the trees because of a maintenance need and confirmed Trump was not involved in the decision. We contacted the Kennedy Center to ask when it cut down the weeping willows and whether it had any plans to replace the trees, but did not receive a response by the time of publication. A White House spokesperson referred our request for comment to the Kennedy Center. Citing a spokesperson for the Kennedy Center, Newsweek reported that the center removed its weeping willow trees in October 2025. Snopes found one image published by Reuters that showed weeping willows at the Kennedy Center in September 2025 and a geo-tagged image from Google that showed at least one such tree cut down in October, supporting this reported timeline. The neighborhood blog PoPville, which covers Washington, D.C., reported on the removal of the weeping willows on October 14, 2025. Snopes could not view metadata for the images in order to establish their authenticity, but had no reason to believe they were inauthentic. What we know about the trees Floca told a Washington, D.C. district court on April 29, 2026, that the weeping willows at the Kennedy Center had to be removed because they were in poor health. He said (Page 28): Ninety percent of the trees were decaying and every time there was a heavy wind or rain a tree would fall down. If you walk around the center at that time, you would see limbs falling and trees falling down. When asked whether he discussed what tree would replace the weeping willows with the Kennedy Center chairman (meaning Trump), Floca said (Page 28): We haven't specifically talked about the weeping willows or the replacement. I think that a weeping cherry tree would be perfect. But we are going to come up with a complete landscape — a comprehensive landscape plan that doesn't only talk to the planters and the willow trees, and that will be part of the plan, the replacement. As of this writing, it was unclear what tree would replace the weeping willows, which lawyer Abbe David Lowell claimed were meant to represent "the grief of the nation" for the death of former U.S. President John F. Kennedy (Page 27). Trump posted digital renderings of his suggested "new, highly improved" Kennedy Center in March 2026 that replaced the weeping willows with either pink or orange-leafed trees. Though weeping willows change color in the fall, their leaves turn yellow or gold, not orange, red or pink like the trees in Trump's renderings, which appeared to suggest the president wanted to replace the weeping willows with a different kind of tree. Floca's testimony was part of a lawsuit brought by several conservation groups that sought to stop Trump and the Kennedy Center's board from carrying out proposed renovations without third-party review. On May 29, a federal judge denied the conservation groups' request for a preliminary injunction that would stop the renovations while the court case was ongoing. Nonetheless, the center remained open at the time of this writing, despite Trump initially saying it would close on July 4, 2026, for renovations. For further reading, Snopes previously investigated whether Trump cut down dozens of cherry trees in Washington, D.C., to make way for a golf course.

title: What to know about EPA approving pesticide trifludimoxazin
label: Rating: Mostly True About this rating
text: Claim: U.S. President Donald Trump's Environmental Protection Agency approved the use of the pesticide trifludimoxazin, a known carcinogen and a PFAS "forever chemical." Rating: Mostly True About this rating What's Undetermined The EPA classified trifludimoxazin as having "suggestive evidence of carcinogenic potential," which essentially means that while there is evidence the chemical could potentially be one that causes cancer, there isn't enough data to say for sure. Additionally, the EPA does not consider trifludimoxazin a PFAS, though the intergovernmental Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development does. In late summer 2026, some people on social media claimed that U.S. President Donald Trump's administration approved the use of a potentially carcinogenic pesticide that's a "forever chemical," also known as PFAS. PFAS, an abbreviation for perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances , are long-lasting chemicals that persistently remain in the environment, capable of accumulating in things like rivers, plants, animals and people's bodies, that often have harmful health effects on people, according to the Environmental Protection Agency . For example, one Facebook post ( archived ) claimed that the EPA "just approved a carcinogenic herbicide called trifludimoxazin," to be used on crops including corn, wheat, oats, soybeans, peanuts, citrus fruits (including oranges), apples and tree nuts such as almonds. According to the post, environmental groups consider trifludimoxazin a PFAS pesticide and "forever chemical." The post began: The U.S. EPA just approved a carcinogenic herbicide called trifludimoxazin for agricultural use on a wide range of crops, including corn, wheat, oats, soybeans, peanuts, citrus fruits (including oranges), apples, and tree nuts such as almonds. Trifludimoxazin is also considered by many environmental groups to be a PFAS pesticide because it contains highly fluorinated chemical structures and can break down into persistent fluorinated compounds - i.e. nature can't break it down properly as it's synthetic. Environmental organizations have described it as a "forever chemical" and have filed lawsuits challenging the EPA's approval. Environmental groups have also pointed out that the company's own studies showed evidence suggesting cancer concerns and that the EPA downplayed those findings whe not was approved. The EPA claims the product is safe and that people shouldn't be concerned. Not a good look for MAHA. Similar Facebook ( archived ) posts ( archived ) shared the same claims, which were also spread on X ( archived ) and Reddit ( archived ). Snopes readers searched the site and sent us emails asking if the rumor is true. The Trump administration's EPA proposed approving trifludimoxazin in June 2025 and went through with the approval in June 2026. Researchers have found some evidence suggesting the chemical may be carcinogenic, but it's not a "known carcinogen" like some posts claim. Trifludimoxazin is a PFAS as defined by the intergovernmental Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, although not as defined by the more narrow EPA definition. Therefore, we've rated the claim mostly true. Trifludimoxazin is a pesticide, specifically an herbicide, that kills certain broad-leafed plants and grass weed species at agricultural sites farming "row crops (e.g., cereal grains, legumes, soybean) and tree orchards and groves (citrus, pome fruits, and tree nuts)," according to the EPA (PDF Page 6). This wasn't the first time the EPA has tried to approve trifludimoxazin. In 2021, while Joe Biden was president, the EPA approved pesticide products containing trifludimoxazin, however; this approval was halted by lawsuits filed by environmental groups. The EPA then changed rules to require further EPA assessments before approving a new pesticide, and, ultimately, the makers of trifludimoxazin dropped their request for approval at the time. The same environmental groups are attempting to halt the new approval for trifludimoxazin through lawsuits, as they did previously. Potential carcinogen The EPA did find evidence suggesting trifludimoxazin could possibly be carcinogenic, although it did not do enough research to confirm with certainty whether the chemical is carcinogenic. In one study of rat carcinogenicity through chronic dietary exposure ( PDF Page 8 ), the EPA found "suggestive evidence of carcinogenic potential." According to the EPA, such a classification means that the data raises a concern that the chemical has "potential carcinogenic effects in humans," but the EPA has determined the data is "not sufficient for a stronger conclusion." Trifludimoxazin's entry on the pesticides properties database maintained by the U.K.-based University of Hertfordshire says that the chemical is "known not to cause a problem" as a carcinogen. The entry does report that trifludimoxazin is a potential liver toxicant, though. The database also notes "no serious health implications have been identified" with trifludimoxazin. So while trifludimoxazin could potentially be a carcinogen, there currently isn't enough evidence to say with certainty that the chemical causes cancer. Forever chemical There are at least three definitions of PFAS , according to a 2022 paper in the peer-reviewed journal Digital Discovery: a broader definition from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development that is widely used internationally , a narrower definition used by the EPA and a definition that is a compromise between the two other definitions. Trifludimoxazin meets the OECD's broader definition, according to the chemical's listing on PubChem . Trifludimoxazin does not meet the EPA's 2023 definition of PFAS . The University of Hertfordshire's database also classifies trifludimoxazin as a PFAS. Where else has it been approved? According to the University of Hertfordshire's database, trifludimoxazin has not been approved for use in the United Kingdom or the European Union. It has been approved for use in Canada . For further reading, Snopes has previously fact-checked claims about potentially toxic chemicals, including a claim about the use of paraquat by the parent company of the pomegranate juice brand Pom Wonderful.

title: Did Olivia Rodrigo donate $10M to abortion organizations? Claim omits key context
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: Singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo donated $10 million to abortion organizations in summer 2026. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True Rodrigo announced she would donate the $10 million proceeds from her Daisy Chain Fields music festival to several organizations. One was Planned Parenthood, which provides reproductive healthcare, including abortions. Other recipients advocate for reproductive healthcare and defend it in courts, although they do not provide abortion services themselves. However ... What's False ... the list of recipients also included a number of organizations that do not have any involvement with abortion. In addition, philanthropist Melinda French Gates pledged to match the proceeds, doubling the total amount to $20 million. What's Undetermined It was unclear how much of the $20 million total was destined for organizations involved with abortion and whether the money had already reached beneficiaries. We've reached out to the festival's organizers and will update this story if we learn more. In the summer of 2026, a rumor spread that singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo had donated $10 million to abortion organizations after U.S. President Donald Trump cut funding for reproductive healthcare . The claim appeared on Facebook and X . One X post said that based on the alleged amount Rodrigo donated and the supposed cost of an abortion of $580, she was "responsible for the murder of 17,241 babies" ( archived ). (It's worth noting that, according to Planned Parenthood , the actual average cost of all types of abortion is higher than the post claimed.) The claim spread following a music festival Rodrigo hosted on Aug. 29, 2026. It's true that the festival, which had an all-women lineup, brought in $10 million in proceeds that Rodrigo said would be donated to several organizations, one of which was Planned Parenthood, which provides reproductive healthcare, including abortions. Other beneficiaries did not directly provide reproductive healthcare, but advocated for it and defended it in courts. However, the list also included organizations not involved with abortion or reproductive healthcare. In addition, philanthropist Melinda French Gates pledged to match the $10 million Rodrigo raised with the festival, bringing the total amount for donations to $20 million. For this reason, we rated this claim a mixture of true and false information. As of this writing, it was not clear how much of the $20 million was destined for organizations that provide abortions or advocate for abortion rights. It was also unclear whether the funds had been paid out, as of this writing. We've reached out to the festival's organizers to ask for answers to these questions and will update this story if we learn more. The Daisy Chain Fields festival The singer first announced the Daisy Chain Fields festival on June 22, 2026, in an Instagram post that listed an all-women group of performers, including Generation Z favorites such as Rodrigo herself, Chappell Roan, Eli and Katseye, as well as older acts such as Sarah McLachlan, alternative rock band The Breeders, which started in 1989, and 78-year-old singer-songwriter Stevie Nicks. "Daisy Chain Fields features an all-women lineup and 100 percent of the net proceeds will go to charities dedicated to advancing and advocating for women and girls," Rodrigo's Instagram post read ( archived ): The Daisy Chain Fields festival website listed organizations that would benefit from the proceeds of the event. Planned Parenthood , known for providing reproductive healthcare including birth control, screenings and care for sexually transmitted infections, prenatal care or abortions, was one of them. The Center for Reproductive Rights , also listed, does not offer healthcare. Instead, its mission is to defend reproductive rights in courts across the U.S. Meanwhile, the National Institute for Reproductive Rights is an advocacy group dedicated to creating access to reproductive healthcare at city and state level. But among the organizations set to benefit, some had nothing to do with reproductive healthcare or reproductive justice. These included Baby2Baby , a charity that provides essential items to very children living in poverty — it is known, in particular, for distributing diapers, formula and clothing, but also school supplies, backpacks and hygiene items . Another organization poised to receive a donation from the festival was FreeFrom , which helps survivors of gender-based violence build financial independence. The Domestic Workers Alliance , meanwhile, defends the rights of domestic workers. In other words, only a portion of the proceeds was destined to fund reproductive healthcare, including abortion. French Gates gets involved The festival took place on Aug. 29, as scheduled. Near the end of the evening, Rodrigo called French Gates to the stage, announcing that the billionaire philanthropist had matched the amount set for donation, bringing the total to $20 million ( archived ): View this post on Instagram A post shared by Girls In Concert (@girlsinconcert) French Gates confirmed this through her social media accounts. The same day, she posted a photo of herself with Rodrigo, saying she would donate the money through her organization, Pivotal ( archived ): View this post on Instagram A post shared by Melinda French Gates (@melindafrenchgates) For further reading, Snopes has investigated many rumors about abortion , including the claim that Massachusetts legalized abortion "until birth."

title: Did Trump post AI photo of 6-fingered Navy sailor?
label: Rating: False About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump posted an image showing a six-fingered U.S. Navy sailor eating a burger with the caption, "OUR MILITARY EATS THE BEST! Nobody feeds our brave troops better than me. The food is AMAZING--the best military food EVER! Other countries wish they could feed their soldiers this well. TOTAL WIN!" Rating: False About this rating A rumor that U.S. President Donald Trump posted an image of a U.S. Navy soldier with a six-fingered right hand eating a burger with the caption, " OUR MILITARY EATS THE BEST! Nobody feeds our brave troops better than me," s pread online in August 2026. For example, above the purported screenshot of Trump's Truth Social post, an X user claimed on Aug. 30, 2026 ( archived ), " The troops are so well fed, they have grown extra fingers! " Although the sixth finger wasn't visible in the artificial intelligence-generated image, there was also no thumb visible — rather, only five non-thumb fingers. The story spread as Navy sailors and Marines aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier prepared to land after more than 270 days at sea , receiving widespread attention for deteriorating conditions on board — including reportedly running out of food and other essential supplies. The alleged post by Trump read in full: OUR MILITARY EATS THE BEST! Nobody feeds our brave troops better than me. The food is AMAZING--the best military food EVER! Other countries wish they could feed their soldiers this well. TOTAL WIN! (X user @torontobaddy.) The purported post by Trump appeared on multiple social media platforms, including Instagram , Bluesky , Reddit , Facebook and X, where several posts received hundreds of thousands of views. Some users seemed to interpret the rumor that Trump posted an AI-generated sailor eating a burger as true. Snopes readers also contacted us to investigate its legitimacy. We dug into the claim, and found no evidence that Trump posted the image of the six-fingered sailor. Rather, the oldest post we found online appeared on an anonymous 4chan account on Aug. 30, 2026, at 12:25 p.m. ET ( archived ) with the caption, " You could eat like this EVERY DAY if you enlisted." The image appeared on other social media pages — including satirical X account @torontobaddy — shortly after. 4chan users operate anonymously, and we were unable to reach out to the user for more information. Although some later posts cut off the purported Trump post's time stamp, the 4chan post of the image showed it was supposedly published on Aug. 29, 2026, at 6:23 p.m. We searched an archive of Trump's Truth Social posts, and found that on Aug. 29, Trump posted at 5:36 p.m. ET and then again at 10:35 p.m. ( archived ).There is no indication he posted between those two time stamps. We also searched the archive for the words, " Our military eats the best, " and also found no evidence ( archived ). In sum, there is no evidence Trump posted an image of a six-fingered general with a caption claiming that the U.S. military "eats the best." The oldest version of the post appeared on online forum 4chan on Aug. 30, 2026, though the anonymous user did not publicly confirm whether they created the image. Although this particular post was AI-generated and we found no evidence that Trump posted it, we have reported on numerous AI-generated images Trump has posted . For example, he once posted an AI-generated image of himself flanked by security while walking alongside a shackled extraterrestrial being and in another instance, he posted — then deleted — an AI depiction of himself in the likeness of Jesus Christ .

title: Was kindergarten teacher fired over gender lesson? Here's the truth
label: Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating
text: Claim: A video authentically shows a kindergarten teacher saying she was fired for helping students discover their gender identity. Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating In late August 2026, people shared a video allegedly showing a kindergarten teacher saying she was fired for helping students discover their gender identity. The video trended ( archived ) on X with the caption "Kindergarten Teacher's Gender Lesson Video Prompts Firing Debate." Under the trend, a popular post ( archived ) from Aug. 28 featured an earlier clip as well as the video in question. The earlier clip ( archived ), captioned "Helping My Students Discover Their Genders," shows the alleged teacher saying she asked her students, "Who wishes that they were born a different gender?" She says half her class raised their hands, leading her to tell the other children to sit in a corner. The post's caption includes the words, "Might be parody." The second video ( archived ), featured on top in the post below, has the same caption as the first clip with the addition of "Update (I Was Fired)." In the second video, the purported teacher says, while appearing to cry, "I got fired. This is like the worst day of my life. I lost my teaching license, so now these children will never be able to discover their true selves." Other users shared the purported firing video on Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), X ( archived ) and YouTube ( archived ). Snopes readers searched this website to investigate its legitimacy, leading us to first perform reverse image searches of both videos. Those searches led us to determine the clips' source was TikTok account named phoebe! ( @bhoepe ), whose bio — "do i appear to be joking?" — hinted the user shared satire and parody. In sum, the video originated as satire. The user in both videos, who told us in an email we could reference her simply as Phoebe, originally posted the first video ( archived ) on Aug. 21 with a caption containing the hashtags #skit and #satire. The caption jokingly features the words, "next step is reassignment surgery in the nurse's office." The second video ( archived ) from Aug. 28, which received more than 15 million views, also had the #skit and #satire hashtags, as well as comments from users appearing to believe the story was real. Some of those comments received hundreds of thousands of likes. Phoebe confirmed to Snopes her videos are skits. She also told us she's not a teacher and has "never worked in a school in any capacity." Other videos on her TikTok account show her saying she's a kindergarten teacher and keeps cat litter boxes in her classroom (a reference to a debunked conspiracy theory), lost her job as a school nurse and fought a funeral procession — all jokes. "None of my skits are based on real events and are exaggerated for comedic purposes," she said. "Humor has always been a huge aspect of my personality, and even as a kid I wanted to be a comedian." She continued: I made the video as sort of an experiment; I intentionally told a bizarre story. I made the whole thing up. I also put "skit" and "satire" in the caption of the video. I wanted to see if the majority of viewers would go through the trouble of reading the caption or looking at the other satire/skit videos on my account, and, astoundingly, most people seemed to just take everything I said at face value. There were also quite a few larger creators who clipped my video and covered it and intentionally hid the "satire" disclaimer, presumably to get more engagement. I think context matters, but even with context some people still believe it! It's as if I could tell them to their face that it was a joke and it wouldn't change their mind. So, the overall reaction to my video is honestly very concerning, especially with AI advancing and the internet being full of widespread misinformation. I feel I did my due diligence by labeling it as satire, and I think ultimately anything can be clipped and taken out of context by people with ulterior motives, particularly if it fits their agenda. For further reading, we previously investigated a video allegedly showing a mother tearing down a teacher's LGBTQ+ Pride flag .

title: Chef claimed Josh Hawley met twice with male escort. There's no proof
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: A chef claimed U.S. Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., twice met with a male escort. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True It's true that a chef named Joe Gera posted the claim on X in late July and early August 2026. However ... What's Undetermined There was no evidence to suggest the senator met with a male escort. Gera has yet to provide evidence to support his story. In a legal notice sent to Gera and shared with Snopes, an attorney representing the senator called Gera's accusations "false and defamatory," adding Hawley "has never exchanged money for sex, nor has he ever paid anyone to remain silent about sex." The notice demanded Gera retract or correct his prior statements and cease publishing anything similar in the future, warning of the potential of a defamation lawsuit. In July and August 2026, people shared a rumor about a chef alleging U.S. Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., twice met with a male escort . There was no evidence to support the story. For example, on Aug. 18, a Facebook user posted ( archived ), "Chef accuses anti-LGBTQ+ GOP Sen. Josh Hawley of kissing a male escort." The post's meme reads, "Married, MAGA, and anti-gay Senator Josh Hawley facing accusations he was seen kissing a male escort before bribing them to remain silent." (GayFamilyValues via Facebook) Searches of social media platforms found users sharing the rumor on Bluesky ( archived ), Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), TikTok ( archived ) and X ( archived ). Believers of the gossip alleged hypocrisy by the Republican senator. Hawley , who has three children with his wife, has for years opposed legislation and rulings strengthening the rights of LGBTQ+ people. During that time, some critics have lobbed unproven allegations of the senator and other Republicans secretly living as gay men. In sum, a chef named Joe Gera , owner of the Pennsylvania-based caterer Keystone Cue, genuinely posted the allegations in several X posts in late July and early August 2026. However, there was no evidence, such as photos or videos, to support his story. When we contacted Gera for supplementary evidence to support his claims, he answered our questions in X direct messages but did not provide evidence supporting his story. As of now, we've rated this claim a mixture of true and undetermined information: It's true a chef made such a claim, and that claim's veracity is undetermined. Hawley's team said the allegations are not true. In a legal notice addressed to Gera that Hawley spokesperson Madeline Sieren, shared with Snopes, attorney David Thompson, a managing partner with the Washington-based Cooper & Kirk law firm representing the senator, called Gera's accusations "false and defamatory," adding that Hawley "has never exchanged money for sex, nor has he ever paid anyone to remain silent about sex." The notice demanded Gera retract or correct his prior statements and cease publishing anything similar in the future, and warned of the senator potentially filing a defamation lawsuit. We asked Gera if he wished to respond publicly to the legal notice and will update this article if we receive an answer. As we noted in an article examining unsubstantiated claims regarding the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's sexuality, Snopes is not in the business of declaring a person's gender or sexual identity. As of this writing, no credible, publicly available evidence supports the rumor that Hawley is gay. In X posts and messages to Snopes, Gera alleged to Snopes without providing proof that Hawley twice met with the same male escort in 2022 at two properties owned by Gera's former employer: the first time that February at a luxury hotel in Washington, D.C., and then at a Virginia mountain resort in April. He said his former employer did not wish to be named at this time for privacy reasons. Gera said he learned of the alleged Washington hotel encounter from a busboy named Carlos who purportedly witnessed Hawley kissing a man, though he did not provide a last name for us to contact that person for independent corroboration. Gera also claimed to have viewed surveillance footage showing the alleged incident but did not provide proof. In Gera's X posts , he quote-shared Hawley's posts about congressional matters with his allegations about the male escort. Gera's posts alleged that Hawley chased the busboy "into the elevator going back up into the kitchen" and paid him $100 "to keep his mouth shut." Fake image of Hawley with other man As Gera's allegations spread online, so did a fake picture of Hawley supposedly preparing to kiss a man holding a voice recorder. It appears someone fabricated the image by prompting an artificial intelligence tool to alter an authentic photo of a reporter speaking with Hawley in 2019. For further reading, we previously reported about another r umor involving Gera in which he made allegations about the vaccination status of Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky. Gera said he cooked at an early 2022 event the senator attended that required unmasked attendees to provide a negative COVID-19 test.

title: RFK Jr.'s hospice comments referred to fraud, not patients' life expectancy burdening taxpayers
label: Rating: False About this rating
text: Claim: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said people in hospice care weren't dying fast enough and were costing taxpayers too much money. Rating: False About this rating Context Kennedy did not explicitly say that hospice patients cost taxpayers too much money because they received treatment for too long. Instead, he was specifically referring to instances of suspected hospice fraud in California. In late August 2026, a claim ( archived ) circulated online that U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said people in hospice care weren't dying fast enough and were costing taxpayers too much money. For example, independent journalist Aaron Rupar shared a clip of Kennedy speaking on X and wrote , "RFK Jr complains that people in hospice aren't dying quick enough and therefore cost too much money." Similar claims about Kennedy's alleged comments on people receiving hospice care also circulated on Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), Threads ( archived ), Bluesky ( archived ) and Reddit ( archived ). Snopes readers contacted us about the claim. Though Kennedy did speak about hospice care during an appearance on the Fox News program "Saturday in America" on Aug. 29, summaries such as Rupar's on X did not accurately reflect his words. Kennedy did not explicitly say that hospice patients cost taxpayers money because they received treatment for too long. Rather, he said hospices in California had fraudulently received federal funds, pointing to billing for patients over multiple years instead of the typical several months as one example. In August 2026, The Associated Press reported on one incident of fraud where a California hospice billed Medicare for a healthy 71-year-old woman. In a recording of the "Saturday in America" town hall featuring Kennedy, he said (at 52:52): We closed down thousands of hospices in California, they didn't have patients, they were just billing us. And the way we found them is because the patients would never die. And so, we could see, we've been paying for this guy for five years — usually, if you go to a hospice, it means you've got three months left to live — these people were never dying, they just had the patient numbers and we were being charged $6,000 a month and just paying, I think 8,000 of them, of these hospices. We're talking about tens of billions of dollars stolen every year. Given the above, we find claims that Kennedy said hospice patients weren't dying fast enough and costing taxpayers money false. Instead, he was specifically referring to instances of suspected hospice fraud. We contacted the Department of Health and Human Services to ask when it closed the 8,000 hospices Kennedy mentioned and how much money the department estimated hospice fraudsters had received and await a reply. Medicare , the U.S. federal health insurance program for people 65 and older, covers hospice care for eligible patients. According to Medicare's website , a patient is eligible if one or more doctors certify they are terminally ill, with a life expectancy of six months or less — not three, as Kennedy said. The insurance program covers hospice care for two initial 90-day periods and successive unlimited 60-day periods. Vice President JD Vance's anti-fraud task force, which President Donald Trump established in March 2026, has focused on hospice fraud through Medicare. The Associated Press reported in August 2026 that fraudsters opened fake hospices and tricked real patients into enrolling, or stole people's identities to bill Medicare for hospice services they did not receive. In May 2026, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services announced six-month moratoriums on Medicare enrollment for hospices and home health agencies. The centers said they had worked with Vance's anti-fraud task force to suspend federal payments to 800 hospices and home health agencies suspected of fraud in Los Angeles. The suspected fraudulent companies received $1.4 billion in Medicare payments in 2025, according to the news release. The release noted that hospice fraud was especially prevalent in Arizona, California, Georgia, Ohio, Nevada and Texas. California's Department of Justice described hospice fraud as "an epidemic" in the state. The department said it carried out its own investigations into hospice fraud within Medi-Cal, California's state-level health insurance program and that it had secured 51 "hospice related convictions" since 2021. For further reading, Snopes routinely investigates claims about Medicare .

title: Does video show elephant rescuing man from Nepal floods?
label: Rating: False About this rating
text: Claim: Footage depicting an elephant rescuing a man from floodwaters was taken during August 2026 flooding in Nepal. Rating: False About this rating Context Since we were unable to identify the video's original source, we could not definitively confirm its authenticity. However, the clip predated the August 2026 flooding in Nepal and displayed visual inconsistencies that pointed to AI generation. As Nepal suffered from catastrophic flooding that left more than 900 people dead and thousands of others missing in late August 2026, a video appearing to show an elephant wading into floodwaters to rescue a man and carrying him to shore circulated online. The video spread on multiple platforms, including Facebook , TikTok , Instagram , Reddit and YouTube , garnering millions of views. Snopes readers also contacted us to ask whether it was real. " In Nepal Elephants were saving people," one X post caption read ( archived ). "What an amazing world we live in." (X user @TonyGunk123.) Several fact-checking sites concluded that the video appeared to be authentic, but it predated the flooding in Nepal and was said to have been captured in India. While we were unable to identify the video's original source for verification, we confirmed that the clip was shared before flooding in Nepal began on Aug. 26, 2026, and displayed visual inconsistencies that pointed to AI generation. The earliest version of the video that we could find was posted to YouTube on Aug. 5, 2026 ( archived ). The video contained multiple anomalies commonly found in AI-generated media . Our analysis of screenshots revealed a lack of detail, harsh or unnatural shadows, inconsistent skin color and texture, degraded quaity, object bleeding and misshapen extremities. (Snopes Illustration.) Although the Aug. 5 video featured a song as the audio, in other iterations of the post, people spoke in the background and yelled as the man appeared to climb onto the elephant. The text over one such video was in Hindi ( archived ), reading "Watch Nature's Display/View" and "How the elephant saved a human" (translation via native speaker). However, the audio was in Thai — further evidence it was not captured during the August 2026 flooding in Nepal. One man can be heard saying "flood" while another woman says, "It's an elephant" before asking, "What is it going to do?" (translation via native speaker). Several commenters on Reddit and Facebook claimed the video depicted a real incident in which an elephant rescued her caretaker as a stunt at an elephant park in Thailand. "The story originates from a genuine, widely celebrated 2016 video filmed at the Elephant Nature Park in Chiang Mai, Thailand," one Facebook user wrote. "The clip captures a real moment where a young elephant named Kham Lha rushed into a fast-flowing river to 'rescue' her favorite human caretaker, Darrick, whom she believed was drowning." Although that story was authentic and KhamLa is a real elephant at Elephant Nature Park in Thailand, the widely shared video of the 2016 incident is not the same video that spread in August 2026. Another article claimed the video was authentic and depicted a real 2017 incident in which elephants helped rescue hundreds of people from a flooded Nepali safari park. We found no proof the video was connected the the 2017 flooding. The image attached to the article was also AI-generated, as evidenced by the man's disfigured fingers and the merging of his arm and shirt sleeve ( archived ). Unlike the 2016 video of KhamLa swimming to her caretaker or the 2017 news reports regarding elephants helping to rescue people, no reputable news outlets reported on the August 2026 video or confirmed it was authentic. In sum, the video appearing to show an elephant rescuing a man from floodwaters is not from the August 2026 Nepal floods. The clip also displayed visual inconsistencies that pointed to AI generation, such as unnatural lighting, texture movement and shapes. For further reading, we confirmed that CCTV footage authentically showed floodwaters destroying the Gyirong Port, a Nepal-China border crossing.

title: Lawsuit alleging rape aboard Navy vessel was dismissed and classified as worker's comp issue, documents show
label: Rating: True About this rating
text: Claim: A civilian engineer working aboard a U.S. Navy vessel filed a civil lawsuit against the United States in 2023, alleging she had been raped on duty, and the court dismissed the suit in 2026, determining it fell under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Department of Labor as a worker’s compensation issue. Rating: True About this rating Claims circulated in August 2026 that a civilian engineer was working aboard a U.S. Navy vessel in 2021 and allegedly raped on duty, for which she later sued the United States seeking unspecified monetary damages. According to the claim, a judge dismissed the case, deeming it an issue related to worker's compensation, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Department of Labor. People on social media platforms spread the report online, claiming that the lawsuit was dropped because the rape was deemed to have happened while in performance of her work duties and was reclassified a worker's compensation issue . Reports about the claims appeared on websites that cover news about the U.S. military as well as in the International Business Times . View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aaron Parnas (@aaronparnas) It was true that a judge dismissed Elsie Dominguez's case because he determined it fell under the Federal Employees' Compensation Act and should therefore be handled by the U.S. Department of Labor, according to court documents . (Snopes generally does not name accusers in sexual assault cases unless they come forward publicly.) The decision cited a prior Supreme Court ruling that determined "unequivocally that FECA is the exclusive remedy for civilian seamen on public vessels." On May 12, 2026, a joint letter from the plaintiff's and defendant's attorneys said that "the Office of Workers' Compensation Programs issued an acceptance " of Dominguez's claim on March 11, meaning the office had decided to classify the rape as a "work-related injury." Snopes reached out to the Department of Labor to ask for documentation of this decision and was instructed to make a Freedom of Information Act request. According to the case docket , Judge Edward S. Kiel dismissed the case on Aug. 11, 2026. Another joint letter from the attorneys, dated one day before the dismissal and embedded below, said "Ms. Dominguez firmly disagrees" with the decision that the assault should be classified as a work-related injury and that she believed it "does a significant disservice to service members like her" but opted not to appeal. As a result, the letter said, "this matter may be dismissed." Sexual assault can be grounds for a worker's compensation claim in particular circumstances, according to some personal injury lawyers . For instance, one New York-based firm said it's possible to sue for worker's compensation when "sexual assault by a supervisor or co-worker when the employer knew about the risk (e.g., through a previous incident) but failed to protect you." History of the case Dominguez graduated from the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy and "excelled professionally and rose through the civilian ranks within Military Sealift Command from 3rd Assistant Engineer to 1st Assistant Engineer, an accomplishment achieved by very few female mariners," according to court documents . The documents said Dominguez met her alleged attacker, the future captain of the USNS Carson City, upon her first assignment out of school in 2014, when he was ranked second mate. She was assigned to the USNS Carson City in October 2021. The alleged perpetrator purportedly initiated a sexual relationship with Dominguez after her transfer to his ship. Dominguez said in court documents that she felt like she could not refuse because he was her superior. She called the experience "demeaning and upsetting" and "told the Captain that she did not enjoy the encounter and did not wish to have any kind of romantic or sexual interactions with him moving forward." The documents described Dominguez as fending off further advances until the situation escalated in December 2021, ultimately resulting in Dominguez's complaint , which she filed on Nov. 11, 2023. The plaintiff's accounting of events stated she was ashore at a bar with colleagues, became intoxicated — possibly drugged — and later woke up in her quarters as she was allegedly being raped by the captain. Stars and Stripes reported that the captain was removed from the ship and criminally investigated ; records show that he surrendered his credentials and the case was withdrawn in March 2025. The civil complaint, embedded below, said Dominguez sought "justice for the sexual assault that she endured aboard the USNS Carson City" on Dec. 21, 2021, as well as "for the failure of the United States to care for her or protect her when she reported the attack the next morning using the proper reporting procedures." The lawsuit sought unspecified monetary damages for Dominguez's experience: As a direct and proximate result of the negligence of the United States, Ms. Dominguez suffered physical and emotional injury, pain and suffering, mental anguish, loss of capacity for the enjoyment of life, loss of future wages and earning capacity, damage to her professional prospects and reputation, and other harms and losses to be proven at trial. These losses and injuries are either permanent or continuing, and Ms. Dominguez will suffer these losses and injuries in the future. The court documents Snopes reviewed on the national legal index PACER included a letter dated Feb. 8, 2024, from Adam Calendrillo, chief of procedures of the Office of Workers' Compensation Programs, who determined "a substantial likelihood of FECA coverage for Ms. Dominguez's alleged injuries." Calendrillo wrote, "Even though the alleged assault occurred sometime in the early morning hours while she was asleep, Ms. Dominguez was under the protection of the FECA 24 hours a day with respect to any injury incidental to her duties." On June 4, 2024, the defendant's motion to stay was granted in part "pending plaintiff's filing of a Federal Employees Compensation Act claim with the Department of Labor and related resolution." We've reached out to Dominguez's attorneys for further comment on the ruling in the civil case and to ask about future plans regarding the complaint. We will update this story if we hear back.

title: Buc-ee's CEO said company is focused on 'conservative, business-friendly' states?
label: Rating: Correct Attribution About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, Buc-ee's convenience store chain CEO Arch "Beaver" Aplin III said the company was focused on building new stores in "conservative, business-friendly" states. Rating: Correct Attribution About this rating A rumor that the CEO of a popular chain of convenience stores in the southern United States said the the company would no longer pursue locations in so-called "blue states" circulated online in August 2026. Users on Facebook and a popular thread on Reddit suggested Buc-ee's CEO Arch "Beaver" Aplin III said the company was focused on building in "conservative, business-friendly states." The quote was correctly attributed to Aplin. The Buc-ee's CEO said it during public remarks on Aug. 17, celebrating the opening of a Buc-ees location in Benton, Arkansas , after being introduced by Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders. Aplin's full remarks are viewable on YouTube . The quote in question began at the 2:11 mark, when Aplin revealed Sanders had asked him to build a Buc-ee's in Arkansas. He said: We're building in a lot of places but when you find a conservative, business-friendly state with a phenomenal workforce, it makes a difference. And I'm starting to realize life's too short to try and build in places that people don't appreciate what you're bringing. Versus a place like this, where people do appreciate what you're building. So that leadership, that concept, that idea of conservative, business-friendly, family-oriented concept, works so much better if it trickles down from the very leadership from the very top at the governor's office. A Buc-ee's news release said the Benton location was the company's 58th store and would create more than 200 jobs for the community. Buc-ee's was founded in 1982 and operates primarily in the South. Local media covered the store opening, including NBC affiliate KARK , CBS affiliate KTHV and the Arkansas Democrat Gazette . The local reports didn't mention Aplin's specific comments nor did they report anything about the chain avoiding blue states. On Aug. 18, Sanders posted a clip of Aplin's remarks to her Facebook page and wrote, "That's why red states like Arkansas are surging and people and businesses are fleeing blue states." Later reporting from The Comeback and Fox Business homed in on Aplin's comments, as well as Sanders' takeaway that the chain intended to stop pursuing locations in so-called blue states. It was these reports that started circulating wider online and got increased media pickup, resulting in the claim gaining popularity. While we found this to be a reasonable interpretation of Aplin's comments, it's crucial to note that Aplin himself didn't explicitly say the company would be "avoiding blue states" during his remarks on Aug. 17. We reached out to Buc-ee's for clarification on the company's plan's for development in red vs. blue states and will update this article if we hear back.

title: Don't believe claim Canadian officials are refusing passage to ships bound for 'Lake America'
label: Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating
text: Previous Article Next Article Article 1 of 4 in Collection Claim: As of August 2026, Canadian officials were refusing passage through the Welland Canal to ships that used the name "Lake America" to refer to Lake Ontario in their documentation. Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating In late August 2026, a rumor spread online that claimed Canadian officials were refusing to grant passage through the Welland Canal — which connects lakes Erie and Ontario — to ships that had "Lake America" listed in their documentation, as opposed to "Lake Ontario." The rumor circulated after U.S. President Donald Trump renamed Lake Ontario to "Lake America" in the United States. Posts on X , Threads , Facebook ( screenshott ) and Reddit claimed Fox News had reported on the alleged Canadian blockade. Snopes readers contacted us to investigate the claim's legitimacy. (X user @MykhailoRohoza) This claim originated as satire. A search of Fox News' archives via its website found no evidence the news outlet had reported on such a claim. Searches on DuckDuckGo , Google and Yahoo also found no relevant and credible news articles reporting on this claim as fact. If Canadian officials really were preventing ships using the term "Lake America" in their documentation from crossing the Welland Canal, it would certainly have made news, and search inquiries would have uncovered evidence of it. The St. Lawrence Seaway Management Corp. oversees ship traffic on the Canadian side of the Welland Canal, which is part of the St. Lawrence Seaway. The Canadian Press reported that Serge Auclair, vice-president of commercial and external relations at the corporation, said vessels are traveling the canal as usual. "Seaway operations are continuing normally and have done so throughout the weekend. Vessels are transiting the Welland Canal as usual," Nicole Giroux, a spokesperson for the St. Lawrence Seaway Management Corp., told Snopes. The earliest version of the claim we found came from an Aug. 28 X post ( archived ) from a Russian X user listed as "Comedian" on the account's profile ( archived ). We reached out to the X user to confirm the account originated the claim and will update this story if we hear back. Many of the earlier versions of the claim shared in English also labeled it as satire, or at least acknowledged its satirical origins. Snopes has debunked similar pieces of media before. For example, in May, we alerted readers to a fake story about Canadian officials denying Trump a $573 billion railway bailout. For more on Lake Ontario, we previously confirmed it was named by Indigenous people, not after the Canadian province of Ontario. Since the effectiveness of satire is subjective , we use " originated as satire " or " labeled satire " ratings based on creators' description of their work. It's your call on whether you agree. title: Yes, Kathy Hochul covered her head while speaking at NYC mosque
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul wore a hijab at a New York City mosque in August 2026. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True Video of Hochul in the mosque authentically shows her wearing a headscarf, with some of her hair visible. What's False Hochul was not wearing a traditional hijab, which is a way of life that involves practicing modesty, covering the head and all the hair. In late August 2026, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul was criticized after she purportedly wore a head covering to a mosque. Videos ( archived ) on Instagram, Facebook , and X ( archived ) claimed to show Hochul wearing a black head scarf or hijab while speaking at a mosque, which conservative critics claimed was disrespectful so close to the anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks. Snopes readers asked us to confirm whether Hochul was wearing a hijab — a covering for the head, hair and neck that is typically worn by some Muslim women. The above video is authentic. On Aug. 28, 2026, Hochul visited the Islamic Cultural Center of New York and covered her head as a gesture of respect as she was speaking in the prayer hall. Hochul has worn a head covering at events with Muslims before and has even spoken out in favor of Muslim women choosing to wear the hijab. She was not, however, wearing a traditional hijab. As such, we rate this claim as a mixture of true and false information. Social media posts and media coverage often erroneously simplify the meaning of "hijab" and claim it is just a headscarf. The term " hijab " has many interpretations but broadly refers to a veil or barrier and is a practice involving modesty for both men and women. Wearing hijab involves modest clothing in an Islamic context, including a head covering. It is worn in many styles but for Muslim women today, the hijab colloquially refers to the covering that typically conceals the head, all the hair and neck while leaving the face uncovered. In available photographs of Hochul covering her head, her hair is visible. She is wearing a headscarf, and not participating in the practice of wearing hijab, as is typically done by Muslim women. Hochul was visiting the Islamic Cultural Center in New York City during Friday prayers. The above video shows her standing before the front wall of the mosque with the decorative glass niche behind her (visible in these videos of the Islamic Cultural Center at 0:23 and 3:29 ). The official Instagram account for the Islamic Cultural Center School — which is affiliated with the Islamic Cultural Center— posted about Hochul's visit and noted that the governor joined for Friday prayers: View this post on Instagram A post shared by Islamic Cultural Center School (@islamic.cultural.center.school) Governor Hochul joined our community at ICCNY for Friday Jumaa, where she addressed the congregation, before visiting the Islamic Cultural Center School of New York. She toured the school, stepped into our classrooms and learned more about the community we are so proud to serve. Hochul is wearing the same outfit in the above Instagram post and in the videos being shared on social media. However, during her visit to the Islamic Cultural Center School, Hochul's head was uncovered . She covered only it when speaking at the gathering at the prayer hall. All Muslim women cover their heads when praying or when inside the prayer hall of a mosque, with some — but not all — in hijab. Given that Hochul was in attendance for Friday prayers at the mosque, covering her head can be seen as a sign of respect. This was not the first time Hochul covered her head at a religious gathering for Muslims. In July 2025, she covered her head when speaking at the funeral of a slain Muslim police officer. In 2020 , she covered her head when speaking at the Jamaica Muslim Center. In February 2024, Hochul posted ( archived ) on X in support of World Hijab Day, writing: "we stand in solidarity with our Muslim sisters who choose to wear the hijab. New York's diversity has always been its strength, and together, we will always promote respect, inclusion, and religious freedom in the face of hate." The post also showed Hochul shaking hands with a Muslim hijabi woman while wearing a head covering. Another Muslim woman in the photograph is wearing a head covering similar to Hochul's: Hochul has not publicly addressed the criticism as of this writing. Snopes has previously covered examples of other leaders wearing head coverings as a sign of respect among Muslim communities, including former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern .

title: Did Trump attack 9/11 memorial in NYC because he wasn't allowed to speak at remembrance?
label: Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York said he wouldn't be allowed to speak at the 25th-anniversary remembrance and that he was "looking into shutting them down permanently." Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating In late August 2026, people shared a rumor alleging U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York said he wouldn't be allowed to speak at the 25th-anniversary remembrance, adding that his administration was "looking into shutting them down permanently." For example, on Aug. 30, an X user shared ( archived ) an image showing the alleged Truth Social post: (@ShawS983 via X) The purported Trump post read as follows: "The National September 11 Memorial and Museum commission decided I'm not allowed to speak at the remembrance. Imagine that? A native new Yorker. The greatest president in history. We're looking into shutting them down permanently, remove the memorial and building a statue of me as tall as the World Trade Center. Not to brag or anything, but I single handedly saved 500 thousand people in those burning buildings. I ran 110 floors at least 50 times within 30 minutes pulling people out of tight spaces. I almost died." DJT According to a reverse image search of the supposed Trump post screenshot, users primarily shared the image on Facebook . It also appeared on the 9GAG meme website. Snopes readers emailed us to investigate the alleged screenshot's legitimacy, asking, for example, "I believe the fact that he won't attend is true, but is this X post for real?" To investigate the rumor, we first checked Trump's Truth Social page and found no such post. We then searched on DuckDuckGo , Google and Yahoo for reports about the supposed post possibly being shared then deleted. If Trump had falsely posted he saved 500,000 people and mentioned plans of building a massive statue after removing the memorial and museum, journalists with reputable news outlets, such as The Associated Press or The New York Times, would have widely reported on it, and our search inquiries would have uncovered such evidence. We found no such articles. While some Facebook commenters questioned whether the post was real, many others recognized the image as fabricated humor, specifically calling it "satire." In sum, the purported Trump Truth Social post screenshot's fake nature and extremely outlandish, false claims, suggested the image originated as satire. We will update this article if we locate the origin of the image. Trump reportedly not going to NY ceremony The story spread in the days before the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, which killed nearly 3,000 people. Ahead of that anniversary, Trump and the White House disputed a New York Times report alleging he decided against attending the New York remembrance because he couldn't speak at the event. The reporting cited three anonymous sources "with knowledge of the events." We did not locate evidence that might conclusively confirm or debunk that claim. A spokesperson for the 9/11 Memorial & Museum previously told Snopes that the organization has historically "intentionally worked to keep the commemoration free of politics because remembering those we lost on 9/11 should never be a partisan issue," and that politicians are not to deliver remarks and must "remain in a designated area." In an authentic post on Aug. 28, Trump posted ( archived ) an attack on Times journalist Maggie Haberman, one of several reporters who worked on the Times' story, calling her "Maggot Hagerman" and writing, "I would love not to speak, because I'm speaking all the time, and this is a day to remember the victims, and their beautiful family members." Trump's post also said he plans to attend the remembrance at the Pentagon. Via email, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Snopes of Trump's plans: As a proud New Yorker, President Trump has spoken about his own experiences watching the horrific events of September 11, 2001. On the 25th anniversary of this tragic day, the President will remember those who were killed at the hands of evil terrorists, honor their loved ones, and pay tribute to the brave first responders who put their lives on the line to rescue their fellow Americans. The White House also said Vice President JD Vance plans to travel to New York, as well as that all three 9/11 sites, including Shanksville, Pennsylvania, will be represented with administration officials in attendance. For further reading, we previously reported about the claim that Trump and hundreds of his workers helped search the rubble in lower Manhattan for survivors after the Sept. 11 attacks. Since the effectiveness of satire is subjective , we use " originated as satire " or " labeled satire " ratings based on creators' description of their work. It's your call on whether you agree.

title: Did Muslim cashier demand Christian boy remove cross necklace? Here's the truth
