title: Detroit police didn't issue warning about gang initiation trend victimizing women
label: Rating: False About this rating
text: Claim: The Detroit Police Department issued a warning about a “gang initiation” trend of young men stabbing women in Detroit in August 2026. Rating: False About this rating Claims that the Detroit Police Department issued a public service announcement warning about a rash of stabbings victimizing women circulated online in August 2026. Facebook users claimed Detroit police said there was a "gang initiation going on in Detroit right now," and the stabbings were allegedly a part of the process. Multiple accounts that shared the claim urged women to "be aware of your surroundings at all times." The claim that Detroit police issued such a warning was false. The Detroit Police Department told Snopes via email that the posts were not accurate. The DPD's website and social media feeds on Facebook , X and Instagram frequently posts alerts and warnings about specific police activity, curfews and community engagement events. Snopes' thorough search of the website and social feeds showed no posts warning about the alleged gang initiation stabbings. A search of Bing , DuckDuckGo , Google and Yahoo revealed no credible reports of stabbings in Detroit linked to gang initiation, which would have been widely reported in the local media if the police had actually issued such a warning. We found reports of two stabbings in local Detroit media in August 2026, neither of which mentioned suspected gang activity. The victim in one report was a male. The other report was about a teenage girl reportedly stabbing a man. It's possible the August 2026 headlines were being misrepresented in social media posts that became an instance of copypasta — a copied-and-pasted piece of text meant to spur further shares — as users began to spread it online. Snopes recently debunked another Detroit-related claim investigating the false claim that Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed ran a "dog slaughterhouse" in the city.

title: World leaders are paying tribute to Dolly Parton. Is North Korea's Kim Jong Un one of them?
label: Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating
text: Claim: Supreme Leader of North Korea Kim Jong Un paid tribute to the late country music star Dolly Parton at the summit of Mount Paektu in August 2026. Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating A rumor that Supreme Leader of North Korea Kim Jong Un paid tribute to the country music star Dolly Parton at the summit of Mount Paektu spread after Parton's death in August 2026. For example, the X account @DPRK_News posted ( archived ) an image of Kim standing on a snowy mountaintop and wrote, "Fond memories of dear friend Dolly Parton immortalized from summit of Mt Paektu." Fond memories of dear friend Dolly Parton immortalized from summit of Mt Paektu. pic.twitter.com/fuUE0K9UGa — DPRK News Service (@DPRK_News) August 25, 2026 The story spread as other present and former world leaders and musicians paid tribute to Parton online. Some social media users ( archived , archived , archived ) seemed to interpret @DPRK_News' post as an authentic message from the North Korean government. Snopes readers contacted us to investigate the rumor's legitimacy. The rumor came from the @DPRK_News X account . That account carries a "Parody Account" label, which X has said applies to accounts that "discuss, satirize or share information." The known parody account has previously convinced several large media outlets to report on its posts as genuine communications from North Korea. Therefore, we find this claim was labeled satire. The photo the page used in its post of Kim looking out over a snowy landscape was authentic but presented out of context. It came from a December 2019 news release about Kim climbing Mount Paektu, the highest peak in North Korea. We did not find evidence in searches on DuckDuckGo , Google or Yahoo that Kim publicly paid tribute to Parton following her death ( archived , archived , archived ). Given the juxtaposition of North Korea's cultural isolation and Parton's global fame, reputable news sources would have reported on Kim's tribute if it were real. The @DPRK_News X account contained other fictitious stories related to North Korea. Some were blatantly false . Others played on current news events , such as a claim that North Korea had entered a trade agreement with Canada. The account's writers, identified as "Patrick Popehat" and "Derrick Popehat" (the two also wrote for the now-defunct blog Popehat) reportedly told Newsweek in 2014 that @DPRK_News' posts were inspired by the real North Korean state news agency and rhetoric used in Soviet newspapers. For further reading, Snopes has previously investigated other claims about North Korea . Since the effectiveness of satire is subjective , we use " originated as satire " or " labeled satire " ratings based on creators' description of their work. It's your call on whether you agree.

title: Beware of alleged Target ad featuring costume that drew backlash for blackface, minstrel imagery
label: Rating: Fake About this rating
text: Claim: A video authentically showed a Target ad featuring a costume that critics said evoked racist blackface and minstrel imagery. Rating: Fake About this rating In August 2026, after the retailer Target removed a costume from its website that faced backlash for evoking racist minstrel and blackface imagery, a video circulated online that social media users claimed ( archived ) showed an ad that Target also pulled featuring the costume in question. The video showed an animated character wearing the since-removed costume advertising various $5 fall deals. One Threads user who shared the video wrote , "Target pulls national ad campaign after accusations that new spokesperson is 'racist.'" "Spokesperson" appeared to refer to the character in the video. View on Threads The alleged ad also circulated on Facebook ( archived ) and X ( archived ), where community notes identified it as a product of artificial intelligence. The video was fake. It came from an X account that described its content as "probably AI" and marked ( archived ) the video itself "Made with AI" on its timeline. Aside from the creator's own admission that they used AI to create the video, it also contained obvious signs of fakery. There were multiple instances of incorrect or unreadable text throughout the video, a classic sign of the use of AI. For example, at 0:01, on-screen text read "HEYY TURGET FANS." It was unlikely Target would misspell its own name in public advertising. At 0:02, the costumed character held a candle that contained misshapen letters in the word "Pumpkin." At 0:05, three products appeared on screen, one of which featured totally unreadable text. (@JasonRink, accessed via X, illustrated by Snopes) The widely criticized costume itself was real. Target announced ( archived ) on Aug. 24, 2026, that it had " pulled an offensive Halloween costume that should never have been part of our assortment." The retailer's statement continued: As a company, we got this wrong, and we are deeply sorry. We know this is especially hurtful for our Black guests, team members and partners. Removing the costume is an important first step, and the company is looking closely at how this happened and what needs to change to ensure this won't happen again. Critics of the costume said it evoked racist minstrel and blackface imagery. Blackface minstrelsy — performances where white performers artificially darkened their faces and depicted Black people as "lazy, ignorant, superstitious, hypersexual, and prone to thievery and cowardice," according to the National Museum of African American History and Culture — are widely considered racist today. Social media users criticized aspects of the costume such as its large, caricatured mouth and the model's pose, which was similar to images of Jim Crow , a blackface minstrelsy character whose name later became associated with racial segregation laws in the U.S. For further reading, Snopes routinely investigates AI-generated content .

title: Trump bought Boeing stock on same day Navy gave company $880M contract. Here's proof
label: Rating: True About this rating
text: Claim: U.S. President Donald Trump bought up to $500,000 in Boeing stock the same day the U.S. Navy awarded the aerospace company with an $880 million contract. Rating: True About this rating Context Trump bought between $250,000 and $500,000 in Boeing stock, according to his financial disclosures. In summer 2026, a rumor circulated online that U.S. President Donald Trump bought up to $500,000 in Boeing stock the same day the U.S. Navy awarded an $880 million contract to the aerospace company. The claim spread on X , Facebook and Threads . Trump's June 2026 financial disclosure indicates he bought between $250,001 and $500,000 of Boeing stock on June 18, 2026. That same day, the Department of Defense announced an $880 million contract with Boeing. Thus, we have rated this claim as true. Historical data for Boeing's stock price indicates that the company's stock actually dropped in price in the days after June 18. The White House has long insisted that there are no conflicts of interest with the president's stock holdings. Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, told Snopes the following in an emailed statement: President Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions. All holdings are maintained in discretionary accounts and invested through computer-based model portfolios that automatically replicate recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000. Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold. All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers. Some of the online posts say Trump bought "$500,000 of Boeing stock." However, the financial disclosure forms don't specify the exact worth of Trump's stock purchases; we know only that it was somewhere between $250,001 and $500,000. The U.S. government routinely awards Boeing billions of dollars in contracts. Trump's financial disclosures indicate that unlike previous presidents, he has invested millions in Boeing and other companies that the government has major contractual relationships with, which ethics experts have criticized due to conflict-of-interest concerns. Showing our work The Office of Government Ethics provides a searchable database of financial disclosures for public officials. A search for "Trump" using that database returned four disclosures published before June. A disclosure added July 1, 2026, titled "278 Transaction" — referring to the office's name for a financial disclosure report — includes the Boeing stock purchase, dated June 18, 2026 (Page 8, No. 206). (Presumably, "BOEING PANY " is a typo and should say "BOEING COMPANY.") (Office of Government Ethics) The Department of Defense also shares a list of contracts announced by date on its " Contracts " webpage. The page for June 18, 2026 , describes the Boeing contract with the Navy (emphasis ours): The Boeing Co., St. Louis, Missouri, is awarded an $880,000,000 firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract that provides for the procurement, modernization, and sustainment of P-8A Poseidon aircrew and maintenance training systems, including the development, integration, testing, delivery, and installation of new training devices and upgrades to existing trainers, as well as associated hardware, software, spares, and support services, in support of Navy fleet readiness and evolving aircraft configurations, mission systems, and training requirements. The P-8A Poseidon is a maritime patrol aircraft. The Securities Exchange Act of 1934 prohibits insider trading , or buying and selling stocks or other securities on nonpublic information. In practice, however, prosecutors must prove intent . For more on financial transactions in the Trump administration, we previously looked into a claim that a Trump insider bet $51 million on oil prices dropping before the United States announced a ceasefire with Iran.

title: Why Dolly Parton declined the Presidential Medal of Freedom 3 times
label: Rating: True About this rating
text: Claim: Singer Dolly Parton declined receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom three times, twice from U.S. President Donald Trump and once from former President Joe Biden. Rating: True About this rating Context Parton revealed she had declined the award from Trump and Biden in a 2021 interview. Their administrations have not commented on her decision. On Aug. 25, 2026, Dolly Parton's family announced the country music star had died at age 80 . In the wake of her death, many people online discussed how she had allegedly declined the Presidential Medal of Freedom — the nation's highest civilian honor — from both U.S. President Donald Trump and former President Joe Biden. Several posts on X claimed Parton declined the honor from Trump twice, without mentioning Biden. By her own admission, Parton indeed refused the medal from both Trump and Biden a total of three times, so we've rated this claim true. In an interview, she revealed she was unable to accept the award for a range of reasons. The Trump and Biden administrations have not commented on Parton's story. In a 2020 interview , former President Barack Obama told television host Stephen Colbert that he was "shocked" Parton had not received the award. He said: "Actually that was a screw-up. I think I assumed that she had already got one. And that was incorrect. I'm surprised. She deserves one. I'll call Biden." In February 2021, Parton appeared on NBC's "Today" to discuss a Super Bowl advertisement in which she participated. Host Jenna Bush Hager asked about Obama's statement, saying, "We read that President Obama's biggest mistake was not giving you the Medal of Freedom, and he said he's going to call his friend Joe [Biden]. Well, have you heard from Joe?" Parton replied: Well, I actually have. To be honest, in all fairness, I got offered the Freedom award from the Trump administration. I couldn't accept it because my husband was ill, and then they asked me again about it and I wouldn't travel because of the COVID. So, now I feel like if I take it, I'll be doing politics, so I'm not sure. I don't work for those awards. It'd be nice, but I'm not sure that I even deserve it. But that's a nice compliment for people to think that I might deserve it. According to Parton, the Trump administration offered her the Medal of Freedom twice, and the Biden administration reached out to her once, leading to her declining it three times. We reached out to the Biden administration in 2025 to learn more but received no response. We also have reached out to the Trump White House for more details. We will update this story if we get more information. Parton, who was beloved across the political spectrum, often shied away from talking about her politics, though she was sometimes critical of politicians in general. In 2023 , she released a song, "World on Fire," in which she criticized politicians on both sides of the aisle, singing: "Don't get me started on politics. Now how are we to live in a world like this? … Greedy politicians, present and past. They wouldn't know the truth if it bit 'em in the a**." For further reading, we have investigated a number of rumors involving Parton .

title: Don't fall for phony recording of Dolly Parton's 'final wish'
label: Rating: Fake About this rating
text: Claim: A video features an authentic audio recording of the late country music legend Dolly Parton revealing her "final wish." Rating: Fake About this rating Following singer Dolly Parton's death on Aug. 25, 2026, people on social media shared and commented on videos allegedly featuring a special audio recording from the country music legend revealing her "final wish." For example Instagram users continued to comment on a video ( archived ) posted nearly two weeks earlier on the Spotlight Hollywood (@spotlighthollywood) account . The Aug. 12 video purportedly features a mix of Parton clips with an audio recording, kind of like a voice-over recording under footage. The post's captions claimed Parton revealed three wishes she hoped to fulfill before her death, though on the audio track she is purportedly heard talking only about "my final wish," that she wished to be buried next to her late husband, Carl Dean. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Spotlight Hollywood (@spotlighthollywood) In the video, Parton supposedly says: I may really not have the chance to see you all again. When you see this video, please remember that this is my final wish before I leave this world. Lately, my health has been getting worse, and I can only stay awake for short periods of time. So, while I still have the strength, I want to take this moment to say goodbye to everyone. Compared to the younger generation of stars, I may not be very famous but I'm already deeply grateful because so many of you, my fans, have been with me all along the way. You've witnessed my growth and my brightest moments and to me you've long been like family. However, as I've grown older, my health problems have become more serious. Maybe it's because I didn't take those mild symptoms seriously at the beginning and now I can only stay in the intensive care unit, enduring painful treatments. Please don't be sad for me. After all, everyone has to go through this stage of life. It's only a matter of time. But if I do leave this world, I hope to be buried next to my husband. At least that way, I won't feel lonely when I go. That is my only wish. And lastly, I hope all of you take good care of your health and cherish the happiness in every single day. I will always love you. In sum, while TMZ did report Parton's family's plans to bury her next to Dean, a closer investigation revealed that although the in-question video's visuals were genuine, the supposed audio recording of Parton's voice was fake. Its creator used an artificial-intelligence tool to mimic Parton's vocals. We found no evidence that Parton ever made the statement heard in the video in any setting. A Google search for some of the text from the transcript located more social media posts but no news media outlets reporting about the alleged audio recording. Had Parton truly made such a recording, news outlets worldwide would have reported it. Further searches of Bing , DuckDuckGo and Yahoo displayed zero results for the same search phrases. Some links that appeared in Google's search results revealed Facebook users sharing the audio, including one video featuring the TikTok watermark for user @hsdpkuabyxt, who posted ( archived ) the fake soundtrack as far back as December 2025 — a time when there was no indication that Parton was in intensive care, as the audio said. We messaged that user to ask if the audio was newly created or reposted from elsewhere. The fake Parton audio contained a hard-to-describe, AI-sounding quality of inauthenticity, not to mention that the AI tool used to create the vocals failed to provide a natural-sounding pause after the words "After all, everyone has to go through this stage of life," instead continuing immediately to, "It's only a matter of time." After Parton's death, some articles featured mentions of her final wishes or requests, for example that of resting in a beautiful bed of plush cotton after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, as well as keeping her Dollywood theme park open in celebration rather than closed in mourning and silence. However, those matters had nothing to do with Parton making a special audio recording. For further reading, we previously reported about the three times Parton declined receiving a very special medal , as well as about the controversy in which TikTok users twisted Parton's past charitable work to criticize other celebrities.

title: Girl Scouts responds to misleading claims about 'Muslim badges'
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: Girl Scouts of the USA offers "Muslim badges" that members can earn by learning the five pillars of Islam or visiting a mosque. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True The National Islamic Committee on Girl Scouting gives Girl Scouts religious recognition awards for learning about Islam. Girl Scouts of the USA allows scouts to wear patches on their uniforms from NICGS and 28 other organizations that give out religious awards. Some of the NICGS patches asked Girl Scouts to learn about the five pillars of Islam or carry out activities in a mosque. What's False Girl Scouts of the USA does not give out awards related to one specific religion. Rather, the organization allows Girl Scouts to wear patches on their uniforms earned through programs developed and administered by independent religious scouting organizations. GSUSA's own faith-related pins are not tied to a specific religion or church. A claim ( archived ) circulated online in August 2026 that Girl Scouts of the USA offered "Muslim badges" that members could earn by learning the five pillars of Islam or visiting a mosque. News of the alleged badges drew anger online, where some social media users pledged to never buy Girl Scout cookies again. One Facebook user wrote : Girl Scouts of the USA has fully surrendered to the cultural invasion by offering badges that require girls to study the five pillars of Islam, tour mosques, and practice Muslim prayer and Ramadan rituals. This is not education. It is the deliberate Islamization of an American institution once dedicated to traditional values and patriotism. Similar posts also circulated on Instagram ( archived ), Threads ( archived ), X ( archived ) and Reddit ( archived ). A number of Snopes readers contacted us about the rumor. The claim contained a mixture of true and false elements. It was true that scouts could earn two types of religious awards . The first, which was the focus of online claims, was a religious recognition program developed and awarded by the National Islamic Committee on Girl Scouting. That program allowed scouts to earn patches for learning about Islam, which GSUSA allowed them to wear on their uniform. Some patches involved learning about the five pillars of Islam or attending prayers at a mosque. The NICGS' program was one of 29 independent programs that also included Catholicism, Judaism, Hinduism and Buddhism. However, GSUSA said in a document about such programs that it did not develop or administer faith-specific religious recognition programs. Therefore, it was false that GSUSA gave out Islam-specific badges or other insignia. GSUSA itself does award a nondenominational pin called "My Promise, My Faith," which invites Girl Scouts to explore "the connections between the Girl Scout Law and teachings from their faith." The organization's programming does not specify that members must learn about the five pillars of Islam or visit a mosque. We contacted Girl Scouts and the NICGS about the online backlash at the Islam-specific religious recognition awards and await replies to our queries. A GSUSA spokesperson said in a written statement on Aug. 26, 2026: Girl Scouts is proudly for every girl. Contrary to misinformation circulating online, Girl Scouts is not a religious organization and does not teach religion. For more than a century, we've welcomed girls of every faith and background. Our national My Promise, My Faith pin invites girls to connect the Girl Scout Law with their own faith. Any other faith-based patches are developed by independent faith organizations, not GSUSA, and participation in these programs is always optional. We will update this report if we hear back from the NICGS. Claims about Girl Scouts giving out "Muslim badges" appeared to originate from posts by Natalie G. Winters, the White House correspondent for the "War Room" podcast hosted by Republican political strategist Steve Bannon. In an X post on Aug. 24, 2026, Winters posted ( archived ) about the "Islamization" of the Girl Scouts through patches and activities promoting Islam. Winters specifically highlighted the NICGS' religious recognition program as well as another patch ( archived ) created by two scouts. Winters' posts did not mention the 28 other religious recognition programs aside from NICGS whose awards GSUSA also allows scouts to wear, nor note that participation in any of these programs was voluntary. We contacted Winters through the "War Room" podcast to ask why she made those omissions and await a reply. Understanding religious Girl Scout patches GSUSA distinguishes between badges , which scouts can earn by following GSUSA's own programming, and fun patches, which Girl Scouts buy or earn by following programming that is not created by GSUSA. Scouts wear insignia, badges and pins earned through GSUSA programming on the front of their uniform and fun patches on the back. GSUSA wrote in its document about religious recognition programs that each religious organization "develops and administers its own program," meaning insignia earned through programs such as the NICGS' would be considered a fun patch, rather than a badge or pin. According to to the NICGS, scouts could earn the Bismillah, In the name of Allah, Qurat ul Ain and Muslimeen awards depending on their age, as well as 11 other fun patches . Through the patches, scouts could learn about Hajj and Salah, which are two of the five pillars of Islam , as well as Jumma Friday prayer. To earn the Jumma badge, a scout needed to attend a mosque for Friday prayers. GSUSA does not require scouts to earn any specific patches, meaning participation in programs like the NICGS' are voluntary. The "All About Islam" patch that Winters featured in her post about the "Islamization" of GSUSA was a project by two junior, meaning fourth- or fifth-grade, scouts to earn a GSUSA award. A website laid out the different tasks various ranks of scouts could complete to earn the patch with an option to buy it at the end. This patch also was voluntary. For further reading, Snopes previously investigated a number of claims about Girl Scouts .

title: Did White House post 'Magic Deportation Bus' graphic?
label: Rating: True About this rating
text: Claim: In late August 2026, the White House posted a "Magic Deportation Bus" graphic to social media, referencing the 1990s educational cartoon "The Magic School Bus." Rating: True About this rating In August 2026, social media users shared ( archived ) an apparent screenshot of an Instagram post by the White House the depicted "The Magic Deportation Bus" in a spoof of the 1990s educational cartoon "The Magic School Bus." Users highlighted the image purportedly uploaded by the White House on Instagram ( archived ), TikTok ( archived ), Facebook ( archived ) and X ( archived ). Snopes readers searched the site wondering whether the White House really posted the image. The claim that the White House posted an image to social media of "The Magic Deportation Bus" is true. Many of the social media posts said the White House shared the image Instagram ( archived ). However, the White House also posted it to other social media sites including Facebook ( archived ) and X ( archived ). The White House uploaded the image with the caption, "Please let this be a normal field trip…" — a phrase commonly said by the "Magic School Bus" character Arnold, a fearful student who generally dislikes the magic field trips Ms. Frizzle takes the class on using the show's eponymous bus. The image posted by the White House appears to combine the Netflix thumbnail for the series with the series' original logo , with the addition five men in handcuffs and ballcaps looking down in the back of the bus. The White House image uses the same background as the Netflix thumbnail. It also uses Netflix's version of the Magic School Bus flying as a rocket with Ms. Frizzle and Liz the lizard at the front, and the words "Blast Off!" written at the front of the bus. The dark blue circle and stars around the bus appear to be an approximation of the same in the series' original logo. The red text outside of the circle is also likely meant to mimic the original series' logo, although it's in the wrong font and is incorrectly placed outside of the circle (the original logo placed the text inside the circle). The inaccurate mishmash of logos is one hint that the image is likely AI-generated, rather than something made by a human editing one logo or the other. Additionally, zooming in on Liz in the White House image shows that the area around Liz's left arm is jumbled and blurry. AI generation tools sometimes struggle with fine, complicated details in images. A White House spokesperson did not answer a question from Snopes about how the image was created. U.S. President Donald Trump and his administration have frequently posted AI-generated images and video to social media that are related to his policies and sometimes reference pop culture. In May 2026, Snopes collected nine examples we've previously fact-checked.

title: Steve Buscemi was hospitalized after NYC attack, but it happened in 2024
label: Rating: Outdated About this rating
text: Claim: Actor Steve Buscemi was attacked on the streets of New York City and hospitalized, as social media users claimed in August 2026. Rating: Outdated About this rating Context Reports that Buscemi was assaulted and briefly hospitalized in New York City were true, but the incident occurred in May 2024 — not August 2026 when the story recirculated on social media. A rumor that actor Steve Buscemi, best known for his roles in "Boardwalk Empire" and "Fargo," was attacked and hospitalized in New York City circulated online in August 2026. People on social media posted images of the actor along with alleged details of the incident. One post on X read, "While walking through Midtown Manhattan, Steve Buscemi was suddenly assaulted by a stranger in what his representative described as a random, unprovoked attack." The rumor circulated shortly after Buscemi was announced to be joining the cast of Apple TV's "Murderbot." (@oniichanph on X) In sum, the claim was true, but the incident occurred on May 8, 2024. The claims circulating in August 2026 were referring to that 2-year-old event, citing it as though it were recent news. The New York Post first reported the attack on May 12 of that year, stating that Buscemi "was strolling through Kips Bay last week when a brute walked up and struck the 'Boardwalk Empire' star in a broad-daylight attack." According to the report, Buscemi "suffered swelling to his face and left eye" and was taken to the hospital. The Associated Press , The Hollywood Reporter , the BBC , CBS News , CNN , Rolling Stone , The Guardian and other mainstream news outlets reported at the time on the attack and its aftermath, including the apprehension of a suspect days later. Clifton Williams later pleaded guilty to assaulting Buscemi and another person he attacked the same day. He was sentenced to five years of probation, according to the New York Post . Multiple outlets published a statement from Buscemi's publicist, who said at the time, "Steve Buscemi was assaulted in Mid-Town Manhattan, another victim of a random act of violence in the city. He is ok and appreciates everyone's well wishes." Snopes reached out to the publicist to confirm the 2024 reports accurately reported their statement and that Buscemi was not hospitalized as of this writing. We will update this piece if we hear back. It appeared the claim began circulating in August 2026 after footage of the attack resurfaced on X , which led to a series of posts by social media pages reporting the incident without any mention of a date. For instance, one such post originated from the popular Facebook page Deadpool Fans , which was operated by a website called We Got This Covered , an outlet known for clickbait-heavy content intended to drive engagement. Their post included a photo of Buscemi along with post text that read: Steve Buscemi received medical treatment for bruising, swelling, and bleeding to his left eye after a stranger suddenly punched him in an unprovoked attack in Midtown Manhattan. Representatives for the Fargo actor confirmed he was treated at a local hospital and is recovering safely at home while law enforcement investigates the incident. A community note was included on this post, pointing out that the incident occurred in 2024. A search of Bing , DuckDuckGo , Google and Yahoo for news of Buscemi being hospitalized in 2026 returned no relevant results from credible media outlets. In 2001, ABC News reported Buscemi was hospitalized after being stabbed in a bar scuffle while filming a movie in Wilmington, North Carolina. The report said Buscemi "was stabbed above the eye and in the jaw, throat, and arm" but treated at the emergency room and released.

title: Rumor has it 'necrophilia brothel' was shut down in Missouri. Don't be fooled
label: Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, police raided and shut down a funeral home in Weston, Missouri, for operating as a “necrophilia brothel.” Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating In late August 2026, a rumor spread online that police raided and shut down a funeral home in Weston, Missouri, for operating as a "necrophilia brothel." For example, a Facebook page called Post Of The Day shared the claim on Aug. 22 ( archived ), adding more details about the alleged crimes. The caption read, in part: Authorities in Weston, Missouri say an alleged necrophilia brothel was shut down Thursday night after deputies received a tip about illicit after-hours activity at a small funeral home. [ ... ] According to investigators, three men were found in separate rooms with corpses in various stages of decomposition. Police said a funeral home employee is accused of organizing the encounters and giving customers access after closing. (Bowlin Media / Post Of The Day on Facebook) The rumor also appeared on Threads, where one user wrote , "I just can't with people! It's getting crazier by the second." Some people seemed to interpret the claim as true. Snopes readers contacted us to investigate its legitimacy. In short, the story is fictional. It originated from a network of social media accounts called Bowlin Media that describes its content as satirical. To determine the rumor's origin, we first used search engines such as Bing , DuckDuckGo , Google and Yahoo . If a major police operation really did bust a funeral home for operating as a "necrophilia brothel," journalists with reputable news media outlets, such as The Associated Press or Reuters, and local publications would have widely reported on it, and those search inquiries would have uncovered such article. That was not the case. The bio of Post Of The Day , the Facebook page mentioned above, says the account is part of Bowlin Media's network. That page first shared the rumor on Aug. 22, 2026 ( archived ). Another page in the network also posted the claim on that date. The "About" section of Bowlin Media's various social media profiles on Facebook and Instagram , including Post Of The Day , reads, "Don't take what you find here seriously, unless you find something seriously funny and if that be the case, carry on." To note its source, Post Of The Day's post includes a faint digital watermark on the lower left hand corner. It shows a "Care Bears"-inspired mascot that features on Bowlin Media's Bipolar Bear Facebook page . That watermark is visible in every post we reviewed. The posts also include the name of a fake news source called "BIPO News," likely intended to be a reference to the Bipolar Bear Facebook page. Further, the image circulating with the posts appeared to be generated using artificial intelligence software. Scanning the image on AI-detection platforms such as Hive Moderation and Pangram returned results suggesting it was fully AI-generated. It should be noted that such tools are not always reliable. (Pangram) We contacted the administrator of the Bowlin Media accounts for their response to the fact some people mistook the satirical story as real news. We will update this story if we receive a response. Snopes has debunked similar pieces of media before. For example, in early July 2026, we alerted readers to a fake story with comparable origins about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani allegedly being asked not to come back to Katz's Deli, a well-known Jewish eatery, after he supposedly visited the restaurant with pro-Palestine activists. Let us note here: Whether you agree with something being described as satire or parody is a matter of opinion. Snopes is in the business of facts. We label these rumors based on creators' description of them. Your call on whether you agree.

title: Project 2025 recommended culling wild horses. Here's why
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: Project 2025, The Heritage Foundation's plan for a conservative presidency that U.S. President Donald Trump has largely used as a blueprint for his second administration, calls for culling wild horses to cut costs. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True Project 2025 calls on Congress to allow the Bureau of Land Management to "humanely" dispose of wild horses. What's Undetermined The Heritage Foundation's document largely frames culling wild horses as a measure to combat overpopulation and damage to natural ecosystems on public lands. While it mentions the taxpayer cost of caring for wild horses, it is unclear whether the authors considered saving money as a primary reason to propose killing wild horses. After The New York Times published a story in August 2026 alleging that U.S. President Donald Trump's administration was allowing the sale of protected wild horses to slaughterhouses, a rumor spread online claiming that Project 2025 endorsed such actions to cut costs. The claim circulated on Facebook ( screenshotted ), X and Instagram , including via Democratic lawmakers like Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware. Some posts online ( screenshotted ) cited the Times article, which said : Project 2025, a policy paper by the Heritage Foundation that in many ways has acted as a blueprint for the second Trump administration, has argued that the bureau needs to be able cut costs by killing horses and said that Congress "must enact laws permitting the [Bureau of Land Management] to dispose humanely of these animals." It is true that Project 2025 endorses a plan allowing the Bureau of Land Management to "humanely" dispose of wild horses. However, the Project 2025 authors don't frame the issue as a cost-cutting measure. Instead, they argue that culling wild horses could help fix overpopulation and prevent further damage to natural ecosystems on public lands. The document does mention the taxpayer cost of caring for wild horses, but it isn't outright referred to as a reason to kill wild horses. Since it's unclear whether Project 2025's authors considered cutting costs as a primary reason to cull wild horses, we have rated this claim a mixture of true and undetermined information. We reached out to The Heritage Foundation and Dave Phillips, the reporter behind the New York Times' story on wild horses, for more information and await a response. In an emailed statement, the Bureau of Land Management did not directly address our questions about whether the agency has a financial incentive to cull horses. Instead, the statement focused on denying claims about sending horses to slaughter. " The Bureau of Land Management does not sell or send wild horses or burros to slaughter, and allegations that individuals are violating federal law or the terms governing the sale of these animals are taken seriously," the statement said. The agency encouraged anyone with information regarding potential violations to report it to the bureau at 1‑866‑468‑7826 or wildhorse@blm.gov . Snopes previously reported that the New York Times' Aug. 20 story included "very strong circumstantial evidence" but no definitive proof of the Trump administration's alleged use of a legal loophole to send wild horses to slaughter. What does Project 2025 say about wild horses? Project 2025 outlines its argument for culling wild horses on PDF Page 560 of the approximately 900-page "Mandate for Leadership" document, which is available on The Heritage Foundation's website. The full section — which refers to the Bureau of Land Management as BLM — is below (emphasis ours): In 1971, Congress ordered the BLM to manage wild horses and burros to ensure their iconic presence never disappeared from the western landscape. For decades, Congress watched as these herds overwhelmed the land's ability to sustain them, crowded out indigenous plant and other animal species, threatened the survival of species listed under the Endangered Species Act, invaded private and permitted public land, disturbed private property rights, and turned the sod into concrete. BLM experts said in 2019 that some affected land will never recover from this unmitigated damage. There are 95,000 wild horses and burros roaming nearly 32 million acres in the West—triple what scientists and land management experts say the range can support. These animals face starvation and death from lack of forage and water. The population has more than doubled in just the past 10 years and continues to grow at a rate of 10 to 15 percent annually. This number includes the more than 47,000 animals the BLM has already gathered from public lands, at a cost to the American taxpayer of nearly $50 million annually to care for them in off-range corrals. This is not a new issue—it is not just a western issue—it is an American issue. What is happening to these once-proud beasts of burden is neither compassionate nor humane, and what these animals are doing to federal lands and fragile ecosystems is unacceptable. In 2019, the American Association of Equine Practitioners and the American Veterinary Medication Association—two of the largest organizations of professional veterinarians in the world—issued a joint policy calling for further reducing overpopulation to protect the health and well-being of wild horses and burros on public lands. The National Wild Horse and Burro Advisory Board, a panel of nine experts and professionals convened to advise the BLM, endorsed the joint policy. Furthermore, animal welfare organizations such as the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals and the Humane Society of the United States recognize that the prosperity of wild horses and burros on public lands is threatened if herds continue to grow unabated. The BLM's multi-pronged approach in its 2020 Report to Congress included expanded adoptions and sales of horses gathered from overpopulated herds; increased gathers and increased capacity for off-range holding facilities and pastures; more effective use of fertility control efforts; and improved research, in concert with the academic and veterinary communities, to identify more effective contraceptive techniques and strategies. All of that will not be enough to solve the problem, however. Congress must enact laws permitting the BLM to dispose humanely of these animals. As shown above, there is a single mention of the cost of maintaining off-range corrals, which the bureau uses in an attempt to control overpopulation. However, the writers' argument is focused on the supposed benefits of culling wild horses to the animals themselves and the ecosystem, and there's no explicit statement that euthanizing wild horses would cut costs. In fact, earlier in the report, on PDF Page 558, The Heritage Foundation suggests potentially spending more money on reducing overpopulation of wild horses. After describing various ways the Bureau of Land Management might save some money, the authors write (emphasis ours): Those funds can be devoted to reducing the risk of wildfires, increasing recreational opportunities, conserving public lands, and addressing tough issues such as wild horses and burros. It's unclear, however, whether the authors intended for the government to spend more money on culling wild horses, specifically. It appears that the authors may have intended that the Bureau of Land Management spend more money on this issue in the short-term to save money long-term, but that's not plainly stated. An additional search for the phrase "wild horses" returned no results within Project 2025 for proposals that outright call for killing horses to cut costs. For more on Project 2025, see our collection of stories about The Heritage Foundation initiative. Project 2025's proposal compared to current law As we previously reported , the Bureau of Land Management has long struggled with crafting policy that legally, effectively and tastefully controls wild horse populations. I n nearly all states where the bureau tracks wild horse and burro populations, the animals' numbers exceed what the agency deems appropriate for a balanced ecosystem, per the bureau's own data . While Project 2025 calls for Congress to permit the Bureau of Land Management to cull wild horses, technically, the agency already has the legal right to. The Wild Free-Roaming Horses and Burros Act of 1971 — the same act that protects wild horses and burros from "capture, branding, harassment, or death" — allows the federal agency to euthanize excess animals "in the most humane and cost efficient manner possible" (Sec. 1333b2C). However, a 2008 report by the Government Accountability Office found that the bureau hesitated to do this because it was "thought to be unacceptable to the public" (Page 56). The Bureau of Land Management spent $101 million — 66% of its budget — on its off-range corrals and pastures in fiscal year 2024. "BLM has a legal responsibility to manage wild horse and burro populations to maintain healthy herds on healthy public lands. When populations exceed what the land can sustainably support, animals can face inadequate forage and water, declining body condition and other serious consequences," the agency said in its emailed statement to Snopes. For more on the bureau's attempts to control wild horse populations, see our original story on The New York Times' reporting. Snopes reporter Laerke Christensen contributed to this report.

title: Did Yellowstone ravens learn to open car doors?
label: Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, Yellowstone National Park rangers warned the public that ravens had learned to open car doors. Rating: Labeled Satire About this rating A rumor that Yellowstone National Park rangers warned the public that ravens at the park had learned how to open car doors spread online in August 2026. For example, the Facebook page Casper Planet posted shared the claim ( archived ) on Aug. 24: Yellowstone Rangers Warn Visitors After Ravens Learn to Open Vehicle Doors Yellowstone officials are warning visitors to secure and lock vehicle doors after ravens reportedly learned how to open several different types of vehicles and push button hatch backs. Rangers say the birds have mostly taken snacks and small objects, although one visitor reported returning to find a raven sitting inside the car on the steering wheel. Park officials recommend locking cars whenever possible and absolutely do not recommend attempting to negotiate with the ravens. Variations of the rumor also spread on LinkedIn . Some users seemed to interpret the rumor that rangers issued a warning about ravens as true, and Snopes readers contacted us in search of more information. To investigate the rumor's legitimacy, we first used search engines such as DuckDuckGo , Bing and Yahoo . If Yellowstone rangers had really released such a statement, these searches would have uncovered such evidence. That was not the case. We did not find any credible reporting about ravens unlocking car doors at Yellowstone National Park. Rather, the Facebook post above primarily appeared as the top result. We identified the rumor's original source: satirical social media account Casper Planet, which describes its output as "Snews that doesn't matter." In addition to a location tag on "Satire Street," its Facebook bio reads ( archived ): Delivering the Snews that doesn't matter directly to your Snews feed. Did we say this is satire? Well it is, names/locations are made up We reached out to the page owner for comment in January 2026 regarding another claim about AI-generated images of massive snow bank on Wyoming's Devils Tower. The account's administrator, Justin Hathaway, told Snopes over the phone: "I just love doing this satire stuff, it's such an outlet for me." He continued: "Another reason is people don't really read things fully anymore, and it's a good way to educate people on reading stories fully if they sound somewhat unbelievable." In sum, while ravens are notoriously intelligent and several species do live in Yellowstone National Park, there is no evidence that park rangers released any kind of public statement regarding ravens opening car doors. Other Casper Planet posts Snopes has debunked include a claim that a Wyoming mountain collapsed and another that a man received a DUI while riding a bear . Because the effectiveness of satire is subjective , we use " originated as satire " or " labeled satire " ratings based on creators' description of their work. It's your call on whether you agree.

title: Did Trump say US was 'dumb' country led by 'very stupid person' one year ago?
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump said, “We were a dumb, stupid country, led by a very, very stupid person a year ago.” Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True On Aug. 21, 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump spoke at a rally for U.S. Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina, where he said, “We were a dumb, stupid country led by a very, very stupid person.” What's False He did not say “a year ago.” Trump was referring to two years ago, when former U.S. President Joe Biden was in office. In August 2026, after U.S. President Donald Trump gave a speech at a rally, social media posts claimed he said , "We were a dumb, stupid country, led by a very, very stupid person a year ago." A meme that circulated on X and Facebook mocked Trump over the alleged remark since he began his second presidential term in January 2025. (Facebook) Trump did call the U.S. a "dumb, stupid country" led by a "stupid person," but he did not say "a year ago." Before making the comment, Trump clearly stated that he was talking about America "two years ago," when former U.S. President Joe Biden was in office. As such, we rate this claim a mixture of true and false information. Trump made the statement during a speech on Aug. 21, 2026, in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. He was supporting the candidacy of Republican U.S. Sen. Darline Graham, sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. We have reproduced that section of Trump's speech below (emphasis ours): And we have people laughing at America as they were just two years ago . We're not going to let that happen. We're not going to let people laugh at us anymore. We're the smart country now, not the dumb country. We were a dumb, stupid country led by a very, very stupid person who wasn't leading. I mean, they had some radical left lunatics leading. He was not leading. And state after state, the Democrat party is now running the most extreme, unhinged anti-American candidates in the history of our country. As seen in the above section, Trump said people were "laughing" at the U.S. "two years ago" rather than "a year ago," as posts claimed. Trump made the comments at the 29-minute mark: Darline Graham was appointed to complete the remainder of her brother's term after his death in July 2026. South Carolinians will vote for the Republican candidate for the senate seat in late August 2026, with the general election taking place in November. For further reading, Snopes has covered numerous false claims about Trump and statements incorrectly attributed to him.

title: Trump posted US is giving 'serious consideration' to changing Lake Ontario's name to Lake America
label: Rating: True About this rating
text: Previous Article Next Article Article 1 of 24 in Collection Claim: A screenshot shows an authentic Truth Social post from U.S. President Donald Trump that says: "The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don’t expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer." Rating: True About this rating Context Two days after making the post, Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename the lake "Lake America." In August 2026, social media users circulated an apparent Truth Social post from U.S. President Donald Trump in which he floats the idea of renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. A screenshot of the purported post circulated on X and Threads . Here's what Trump allegedly said, in full: The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don't expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP Trump did, in fact, make the above Truth Social post on Aug. 25, which can be viewed on his account ( archived ). The White House also shared the screenshot on X ( archived ). As such, we have rated this claim as true. Following the publication of this story, Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename the lake "Lake America." The president later shared a map of the area, with "Lake Ontario" crossed out and replaced with "Lake America." Trump's social media posts about renaming Lake Ontario came after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney walked away from negotiations over tariffs amid a contentious trade war between the United States and Canada. "When the Americans go to the negotiation table first with the right attitude towards our industries and a true partnership, of course we'll come to the negotiation table," Carney said . "But an attitude that Canada is a subsidiary of the United States … that's not something we're going to accept." Snopes previously confirmed that Trump said he wanted to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, which he eventually followed through on via executive order . As with the Gulf of Mexico, Trump is allowed to change Lake Ontario's name for official U.S. government use, but he can't dictate what other governments call it. Lake Ontario is a shared international waterway, and Canada and the United States jointly manage it through multiple agreements . For more on the United States and Canada's relationship under Trump, we broke down the U.S. president's threats to annex the country's northern neighbor. title: Image allegedly shows baby in car seat suspended outside vehicle. Is it real?
label: Rating: Fake About this rating
text: Claim: An image authentically shows a baby sitting in a car seat hanging from the open window of a driver's side door. Rating: Fake About this rating Context Someone generated the image with AI. Genuine vintage photos do exist showing children in car seats suspended outside the driver's side doors of parked vehicles. Despite social media speculation, no historical records indicate people drove cars with children in a seat hanging outside of the vehicle, nor does data suggest parents or guardians left kids hooked onto the door to avoid interior car heat while adults shopped. In summer 2026, people claimed a image spreading online was a vintage photo of a baby sitting in a car seat suspended outside the driver's door: (zadraaa accessed via Reddit) In the example above, posted June 7, a Reddit user captioned ( archived ) the image, "A 1950s-style baby car seat, reminding us how far safety standards have come. Never leave a child in a hot car while you shop." The black-and-white image shows a baby suspended in a car seat outside the open window of the driver's door of the vehicle. A house with a stoop and striped awnings is visible in the background. Other users shared the picture on Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), Reddit ( archived ) and X ( archived ). In short, the image is fake, generated using artificial intelligence. That said, genuine vintage photos do exist showing children sitting in external car seats hanging on the doors of parked cars . Signs of AI in the fake car seat image The fake car seat image displays numerous signs that generative AI was used to create it. The full-size version has an unusual crispness for photographs from the 1940s and '50s. As seen in a reflection on the the car's body, the child appears to have three legs and feet (marked 1, 2 and 3 below): Notice, too, that the car seat is padded on the child's right side, but there appears to be no padding on the side closest to the car. Also, if the seat were removed from the door as configured and attached to a seat inside the car, the child would be facing left or right, not forward. Our research found only vintage car seats designed to face forward or backward. Speaking of facing forward, the full-size image shows the car parked perpendicular to the curb instead of parallel to it as would be more expected in a residential neighborhood. The right side of the house in the background (as seen from the street) appears to have an odd mixture of brick and vinyl siding. Had the brick formed into a fireplace and chimney, that might make sense. However, there are windows on that wall, likely indicating no fireplace. (A Reddit user noted ( archived ) several of these signs of AI.) Multiple scans of the image with the Google Gemini AI tool returned the same conclusion. Gemini detected the company's invisible SynthID watermark , meaning someone used a Google-created AI tool to create the image: "My analysis of this image indicates that it contains a SynthID watermark, which means that most or all of the content was edited or generated with Google AI." A reverse image search failed to find any posts with the fake image prior to a March 2026 post ( archived ) on the Historical Image Facebook page , on which managers shared nothing but content labeled as AI-generated. Snopes messaged the page's managers to ask for more information about the creation of the image. As of this writing, the page has posted no new content since June. Real pictures of children in car seats suspended outside cars Reverse image searches did locate similar images that were genuine, i.e., not created with AI or digitally edited. For example, on Aug. 2, 2026, an Instagram user posted ( archived ) the fake image alongside an authentic photo showing a boy in a car seat suspended outside the door of a parked vehicle. The caption alleged, without evidence, that people would drive with the child unsafely attached outside the car to "enjoy the view during road trips." (@explaining.tech accessed via Instagram) A popular Facebook post ( archived ) from 2021 showing the same genuine picture from the above post featured a user claiming, also without proof, that people would hook a child car seat outside on a car door to avoid leaving a child inside a hot car while adults shopped. (A house in the background features a striped awning similar to the AI-generated image. The Google AI tool that created the fake image potentially referenced this genuine photo.) (American Hot Rodders Show accessed via Facebook) The car seat in the authentic photo appears to match the Peterson car seat that appeared in a 1955 newspaper advertisement ( archived ). It cost $3.45. (Stockton Record via Newspapers.com) Another authentic picture, which appeared in a 2018 Reddit post ( archived ), also showed a young boy in a car seat hanging outside a car door. The caption reads, "Early model of a baby car seat." There are others in the picture as well, including a young girl smiling, left, and what appear to be the shadows of two adults on the right side. (H_G_Bells accessed via Reddit) A 1945 newspaper ad ( archived ) displays an illustration of the same or a similar brand of car seat as that pictured immediately above, priced at $1.98. The ad reads in part, "This one slips right over the regular car seat back." (St. Louis Star Times via Newspapers.com) Further reverse image searches located websites, for example vintag.es , hosting authentic vintage photos of children seated forward or backward, not left or right, in car seats inside cars. How we located brands and illustrations For readers interested in our research process, we found past car seat brands and the above-shown advertising illustrations via a path of online searches. A Google search for the history of car seats led to an article mentioning the Bunny Bear company. A Newspapers.com search for "Bunny Bear," with quotation marks, as well as the terms "car," "seat" and "baby," led us to a vintage ad ( archived ) mentioning the Rose Derry company. A Newspapers.com search for "Rose Derry" and "car seat" pointed to another vintage ad ( archived ) listing numerous children's product brand names. Searches for those brands led to other leads, including the aforementioned car seat ads with illustrations, as well as numerous illustrated patents . For further reading, we previously investigated alleged vintage photos showing babies in cagelike enclosures outside apartment-building windows.

title: Was George Clooney 'very upset' about Mamdani's NYC wealth tax?
label: Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating
text: Claim: In August 2026, actor George Clooney was "very upset" about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's wealth tax, saying "it’s gotten way out of hand." Rating: Originated as Satire About this rating In August 2026, a rumor spread online that actor George Clooney was "very upset" about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's wealth tax on second homes in the city, allegedly saying "it's gotten way out of hand." For example, on August 17, one X user posted a screenshot featuring the claim, which included text that read ( archived ): George Clooney's $25+ million penthouse in NYC is technically his "second home," because whenever he comes to NYC to shoot or direct, he uses this residence—and therefore it falls under Mamdani's wealth tax. Mr. Clooney is apparently very upset about Mamdani's wealth tax. He said in a podcast that he does a lot of charity work and considers himself exempt from the wealth tax, but he still received a letter from the Mamdani government demanding that he pay it. Mr. Clooney said, "I voted for Mamdani to help out the poor and was ready to bear a little communism, but it's gotten way out of hand." (X) The story spread as wealthy New Yorkers pushed back against Mamdani's "Pied-à-Terre Tax," claiming its rollout has been disorganized. The tax aims to target those who own second homes worth $5 million or more. Mamdani's office received particular backlash after the Department of Finance published a list naming all property owners who would potentially be required to pay the tax, including celebrities like former Vogue editor Anna Wintour and actor Cynthia Nixon, a vocal Mamdani supporter. Although Clooney and his wife, Amal Clooney, reportedly purchased a luxury apartment in Midtown, New York City, in 2016, it is unclear whether they are NYC homeowners, as of this writing. Some users seemed to believe the rumor that Clooney was one of the wealthy celebrities resisting the tax. Snopes readers contacted us to investigate its legitimacy. In short, the fabricated story stemmed from a satire site. No evidence could be found of Clooney publicly saying, "I voted for Mamdani to help out the poor and was ready to bear a little communism, but it's gotten way out of hand." Given some posts omitted the satire label when sharing the rumor, we concluded that this claim originated as satire. A Facebook account called The Satire liners first posted the copypasta — that featured in the above X post — on Aug. 16, 2026 ( archived ). T o investigate the rumor's legitimacy, we first used search engines such as DuckDuckGo , Bing and Yahoo to search for the quote purportedly attributed to Clooney. If the actor had really made such a public comment about Mamdani, journalists with reputable news outlets, such as The Associated Press or Reuters, would have likely reported on it, and those search inquiries would have uncovered such evidence. That was not the case. We did not find any credible reporting indicating Clooney said Mamdani's policies had "gotten way out of hand." To note its satirical nature, The Satire liners' post includes a digitally added watermark that is also visible in other accounts' posts featuring the claim. That marking is not visible in every post found online. The watermark features the account's profile image and text that reads, "Nothing on this page is real. If you believe anything we post then you're potato crop." The Satire liners' Facebook bio similarly reads ( archived ), "We post only SATIRE stories. Nothing on this page is Real." (Facebook) The satirical account contains numerous fictitious stories based on real events or people. For example, another post claims actor Denzel Washington said, "Mamdani is pro-communist and supports Sharia law. He has lost his damn mind." For further reading, in August 2026, Snopes alerted readers to a claim with similar satirical origins about shoppers at Mamdani's NYC-run grocery stores requiring a "special mark" on their hand or forehead.

title: Did Trump propose eliminating property taxes for some seniors?
label: Rating: False About this rating
text: Claim: U.S. President Donald Trump proposed eliminating property taxes for people age 65 and older who have paid off their mortgages. Rating: False About this rating Context The federal government does not control property taxes, which are levied at the state and local levels. In August 2026, a rumor spread online that U.S. President Donald Trump proposed eliminating property taxes for people age 65 and older who have paid off their mortgages. People shared the claim on Instagram and Facebook . An X user claimed Trump had already announced such a measure, which would affect "HOMEOWNERS 65+ WHO OWN THEIR HOMES OUTRIGHT" ( archived ): Meanwhile, Snopes readers emailed us to confirm the veracity of the rumor. The claim was false. We found no evidence Trump ever proposed lifting property taxes for seniors who have paid off their mortgages. Furthermore, the federal government does not control property taxes , which are levied at the state and local levels. In other words, Trump does not have the power to lower property taxes for seniors. A White House spokesperson told Snopes via email that Trump "has not stated this." To investigate the rumor's legitimacy, we first used search engines such as DuckDuckGo , Google and Bing . If Trump had made such a proposal, reputable news outlets, such as The Associated Press or Reuters, would have widely reported on it, and those search inquiries would have uncovered such evidence. This was not the case. Instead, it appears people online may have confused federal tax relief measures Trump proposed with ideas for property tax reform. For example, in 2025, Trump's signature legislation, known as the One Big Beautiful Bill , sought to create a "$6,000 bonus deduction for taxpayers 65 and older." The OBBB also raised the federal itemized deduction cap for certain state and local taxes from $10,000 to $40,000. Also, on Feb. 10, 2026, California's government announced an initiative to exempt certain homeowners age 60 and older from paying property taxes on their principal residence if they have lived in it for at least five years, or in California for at least 10 years. Further, Trump was reportedly considering a tax break on capital gains on the sale of property. This claim has not been confirmed as of this writing. Lawmakers in several states have also proposed slashing property taxes amid steep increases in property values. However, none of these proposals or measures amount to Trump eliminating property taxes for seniors. For further reading, Snopes compiled claims about the Trump administration's alleged quotes regarding tariffs .

title: Target removed kid's Halloween costume from website amid backlash over blackface, minstrel imagery
label: Rating: True About this rating
text: Claim: Target removed a children's Halloween costume from its website that social media users criticized as evoking racist minstrel and blackface imagery. Rating: True About this rating In August 2026, a claim circulated online that the retailer Target removed a children's Halloween costume from its website that social media users criticized as evoking racist minstrel and blackface imagery. For example, one Facebook user who posted an image of the alleged costume wrote ( archived ): Target removed a children's Halloween clown costume from its Target website after facing intense online backlash. Critics pointed out that the costume's dark face covering and exaggerated wide mouth resembled historical minstrel and blackface caricatures. The image the user shared showed a Black child wearing orange-and-black striped pants and a shirt with a black hood with a large smile printed on it, a small orange-and-black hat and black gloves. The image showed the child in a "running" pose. Claims that Target sold the costume despite its racist imagery and later removed it also circulated on Instagram ( archived ), Threads ( archived ), X ( archived ), Bluesky ( archived ) and Reddit ( archived ). Snopes readers contacted us about the claim. The claim was true. After sending Target an image of the costume and asking whether it listed, then removed it from its website, a company spokesperson replied via email on Aug. 24: As a company, we know we got this wrong, and we are deeply sorry. The costume is offensive and should never have been part of our assortment. It is no longer available for sale. We know this is especially hurtful for our Black guests, team members and partners. Removing the costume is an important first step, and the company is looking closely at how this happened and what needs to change to ensure this won't happen again. According to a since-deleted listing for the costume on Target's website, the retailer originally described the costume as a "Circus Glow Clown Halloween Costume." We asked the spokesperson when Target removed the costume. We also contacted a costume store with the same name as the one Target said produced the costume for comment on the removal. We await replies to our queries. Social media users said the costume evoked racist minstrel and blackface imagery. Blackface minstrelsy, which the National Museum of African American History and Culture describes as " comedic performances of 'blackness' by whites in exaggerated costumes and make-up" dates to the 1830s. It involved white performers artificially darkening their faces and wearing tattered clothing to imitate Black people in performances that depicted them as "lazy, ignorant, superstitious, hypersexual, and prone to thievery and cowardice," the museum wrote. Jim Crow, whose name since became associated with racial segregation laws across the U.S., is perhaps the most famous blackface minstrelsy character. One social media user circulated an image of the Jim Crow character beside the photo of the child wearing the Target costume and noted similarities between their poses. The National Museum of African American History and Culture wrote that blackface and minstrelsy were ways in which white people defined and distinguished what it meant to be white from what it meant to be Black. Speaking to PBS' "American Experience," author Mel Watkins reportedly said minstrel shows had a huge role in shaping and perpetuating stereotypes about Black people. He said: It was advertised as a peephole view of what black people were really like. To that extent, it affected all of society because those people who didn't know blacks, and there were many places where there were very few blacks, assumed that those characterizations, those depictions, those foolish characters on stage, were real black people. And so it had an immense effect on the way mainstream society thought about blacks. For further reading, Snopes has previously investigated other claims regarding the racist practice of blackface .

title: Gary Sinise takes fallen soldiers' families to Disney World every year
label: Rating: Mostly True About this rating
text: Claim: Actor Gary Sinise has taken more than 1,000 children of fallen service members to Disney theme parks free of charge. Rating: Mostly True About this rating Context The program is called the “Snowball Express” and operates through the actor’s nonprofit organization, the Gary Sinise Foundation. While some versions of the claim name the specific theme park as Disneyland in Anaheim, California, the Snowball Express actually takes its participants to Walt Disney World Resort in Orlando, Florida, annually. Further, although minimal, participating families are responsible for some costs of travel such as airport transportation and luggage fees. Gary Sinise, the acclaimed actor most known for his roles in "Apollo 13," "Forrest Gump" and "CSI: NY," was the subject of a claim circulating in August 2026 that he takes more than 1,000 children of fallen United States service members to Walt Disney World every year, free of charge. The claim gained traction on Reddit with over 18,000 upvotes, with one user commenting, "This guy and his foundation does more than all the other celebrities combined for our troops and their families." A photo included with the Reddit post depicted Sinise on an airplane surrounded by families smiling and wearing Disney gear. Every year, actor Gary Sinise takes more than 1,700 family members of fallen soldiers to Walt Disney World for free by u/Wonderfulhumanss in BeAmazed The claim that Sinise took more than 1,000 children of fallen service members to Disney theme parks is mostly true. The program is called the "Snowball Express" and operates through the actor's nonprofit organization, the Gary Sinise Foundation . According to the foundation's website, its mission is to honor "defenders, veterans, first responders, their families, and those in need" by "creating and supporting unique programs designed to entertain, educate, inspire, strengthen, and build communities." While most versions of the claim name the specific theme park as Disneyland, located in Anaheim, California, the Snowball Express actually takes its participants to Walt Disney World Resort in Orlando, Florida, each year. Further, while costs are minimal, participating families are responsible for some expenses, such as transportation to the airport as well as parking and luggage fees. For these reasons, we've rated this claim as mostly true. According to the Gary Sinise Foundation's webpage dedicated to the Snowball Express program, the event, held annually in December, is a "a five-day experience for 1,750+ children of the fallen and the surviving spouse/guardian. With special time to honor their fallen and a blend of fun entertainment and inspiring programs, these families can lean on their peers for support." In addition, the foundation's official Facebook page posted a variety of photos from the Snowball Express events throughout the years of its operation. (The Gary Sinise Foundation Facebook page) According to the Disney Parks Blog , "the official blog for the Disneyland Resort, Walt Disney World Resort and Disney Cruise Line," the Snowball Express has origins dating back to 2003. The Disney Parks Blog stated: The Snowball Express has a special connection to Disney Parks. This annual healing retreat began in 2003 when U.S. Army Private First-Class Jesse Givens wrote a letter to his wife before his deployment to Iraq, which included a wish for his family to visit Disney Parks if he didn't return. This wish was fulfilled in 2006 when his family and others of fallen soldiers visited Disneyland Resort. Gary Sinise became involved in 2007, when he and his band, the Lt. Dan Band, performed for these families. "In 2017, the Gary Sinise Foundation took over the program, and the first retreat at Walt Disney World took place in 2018, starting an annual tradition for the families of fallen U.S. military heroes," the blog continued. Since the Gary Sinise Foundation took over the program, "more than 17,000 children of fallen military heroes, fallen first responders and their surviving parent/guardian have participated in the healing retreat," wrote the Disney Parks Blog. In December 2024, "the Foundation brought more than 1,700 family members from more than 90 cities around the nation and overseas, as far as Europe and Guam," they added. "During this five-day healing retreat, the families connected with each other and enjoyed the magic of Disney while honoring the legacy of their loved one's service and sacrifice." One such memorial included a sunrise procession at Disney's Magic Kingdom in which "nearly 1,000 Disney VoluntEARS, including many cast members who are military veterans, lined the streets before 5 a.m. to stand in reverence of these military families for their sacrifices." Most claims shared online also alleged the program was "free of charge" to the participating families. While the heaviest financial burdens of airfare, lodging, meals and theme park passes were covered, according to the foundation's FAQ page about the program, attending families are responsible for the costs related to travel to and from the airport as well as parking and luggage fees. The organization thanked "the generosity of the American public, our partners, donors, and volunteers" for covering a bulk of the cost. The same FAQ page said the program "serves the children (and surviving spouse or guardian) of fallen military heroes and first responders, who served on or after Sept. 11, 2001, with a service-related death occurring on or after Sept. 11, 2001." We've reached out to the Gary Sinise Foundation for further comment on the Snowball Express and will update this article if we receive a response.

title: Did activist Marion Stokes record more than 300K hours of news footage?
label: Rating: Mixture About this rating
text: Claim: Activist Marion Stokes recorded more than 300,000 hours of news footage from the 1970s to her death in 2021. Rating: Mixture About this rating What's True Stokes recorded television news for more than three decades, amassing a collection of more than 70,000 tapes. What's Undetermined The duration of her recordings has not been definitively established. In 2026, posts on social media sites highlighted an important historical figure: activist Marion Stokes. The posts claimed Stokes recorded around 300,000 hours of television — purportedly one of the largest known personal archives of such material. The claim circulated on TikTok , Reddit and Threads . A TikTok video claimed to detail her remarkable life: Marion Stokes started recording television in 1979 because she noticed something that bothered her deeply. TV networks were erasing their own archives — wiping old footage to save money and storage space. Nobody was keeping the record. So she decided she would. For 35 years, she ran up to eight VCRs simultaneously in her Philadelphia home, recording around the clock. News, commercials, sitcoms, local broadcasts, breaking events. The tapes ran out every six to eight hours. She almost never missed a change. Friends and family described rushing home from dinner so she could swap them out.
